title: 胡佛水壩的建設與意義（Construction and Significance of Hoover Dam）
paras: Located in Black Canyon straddling the border between Nevada and Arizona in the southwestern region of the United States, Hoover Dam is named one of the Top 10 Construction Achievements of the 20th century. The dam, constructed between 1931 and 1936, was the largest of its kind at the time. Its construction was the result of a massive effort involving thousands of workers and cost over one hundred lives.

Since about 1900, the Black Canyon and nearby Boulder Canyon had been investigated for their potential to support a dam that would control floods, provide irrigation water, and produce hydroelectric power. In 1928, the US Congress authorized the project. The winning bid to build the dam was submitted by Six Companies, Inc. However, such a large concrete structure had never been built before, and some of the techniques were unproven. The extreme summer heat and lack of facilities near the site also presented tremendous difficulties. Nevertheless, Six Companies turned over the finished dam to the federal government on March 1, 1936, more than two years ahead of schedule.

The initial design of the dam, which was more concerned with the dam’s functionality than its exterior, was criticized by many as being too plain and unremarkable for a project of such immense scale. So Gordon B. Kaufmann, the architect who was brought in to redesign the exterior, greatly streamlined the design and applied an elegant Art Deco style to the entire project. Allen Tupper True, an American illustrator, was also hired to handle the design and decoration of the walls and floors of the new dam. He integrated into his design the images and colors based on Native American visions of rain, lightning, clouds, and animals, thereby creating symbolic patterns which appear both ancient and modern.

Today, Hoover Dam has become a national historic landmark. Standing at more than 725 feet above the Colorado River, the highest concrete dam in the Western Hemisphere continues to draw crowds 85 years after its creation, attracting more than a million visitors a year.

outline: 胡佛水壩位於美國內華達州和亞利桑那州交界的黑峽谷，名列 20 世紀十大營建成就，1931 到 1936 年興建，是當時最大的水壩，超過一百名工人喪命。
(Since about 1900) 大約從 1900 年起，黑峽谷一帶就在評估興建水壩，用來防洪、灌溉和水力發電；1928 年美國國會核准，由 Six Companies 公司得標。
(However) 然而這麼大的混凝土結構前所未有，夏天又酷熱，困難重重；(Nevertheless) 儘管如此，Six Companies 在 1936 年 3 月 1 日完工，比預定早了兩年多。
最初的設計太平淡，(So) 所以請建築師 Kaufmann 重新設計外觀，採用裝飾藝術風格；插畫家 Allen Tupper True 融入美洲原住民的意象，(thereby) 創造出既古老又現代的圖案。
(Today) 如今胡佛水壩已是國家歷史地標，高出科羅拉多河 725 英尺以上，是西半球最高的混凝土水壩，完工 85 年後每年仍吸引超過一百萬名遊客。

zh: 胡佛水壩位於美國西南部，坐落在內華達州和亞利桑那州交界的黑峽谷，名列 20 世紀十大營建成就之一。這座水壩在 1931 年到 1936 年間興建，在當時是同類建築中最大的。興建工程動員了數千名工人，也有超過一百人在工程中喪命。

大約從 1900 年起，就有人在評估黑峽谷和附近的博爾德峽谷適不適合興建水壩，用來防洪、提供灌溉用水和水力發電。1928 年，美國國會核准了這項工程，由 Six Companies 公司得標興建。不過，這麼大的混凝土結構以前從來沒有人蓋過，有些施工技術也還沒有經過驗證。再加上夏天酷熱，工地附近又缺乏設施，困難重重。儘管如此，Six Companies 還是在 1936 年 3 月 1 日把完工的水壩交給聯邦政府，比預定時間早了兩年多。

水壩最初的設計重視功能，不太講究外觀，很多人批評，以這麼大規模的工程來說，這個設計太平淡、太普通了。於是，建築師 Gordon B. Kaufmann 受邀重新設計外觀，他把造型大幅簡化成流線型，整個工程都採用優雅的裝飾藝術（Art Deco）風格。美國插畫家 Allen Tupper True 也受聘負責新水壩牆面和地板的設計與裝飾。他把美洲原住民對雨、閃電、雲和動物的想像，連同相關的圖像和色彩，融入自己的設計，創造出既古老又現代的象徵圖案。
如今，胡佛水壩已經成為國家歷史地標。這座西半球最高的混凝土水壩，高出科羅拉多河 725 英尺以上，完工 85 年後仍然吸引大批人潮，每年有超過一百萬名遊客造訪。

title: 餐廳的起源與發展（The Origin and Development of Restaurants）
paras: France gave birth to restaurants, but it was no civilized affair. In fact, today’s restaurant business is a byproduct of the class warfare that arose during the French Revolution.

Back in the Middle Ages, fine dining was a privilege enjoyed exclusively by noble families who had their own grand kitchens and personal chefs. The only commercial diners for the masses were dusty, shabby roadside inns, where strangers crowded around mediocre buffets of lukewarm roasts and over-sauced beans. But sometime in the 1760s, the merchant class of Paris developed a taste for healthy clear broths which were considered restorative; hence the term “restaurant.” By the 1780s, this new Parisian “healthy food” craze led to a handful of reputable dining halls, where customers could sit at individual tables and choose from a wide range of dishes.

Ironically, the popularity of these restaurants grew at a time when the majority of the French population could not afford bread. Decades of harsh winters and oppressive taxation had taken their toll on kitchen tables. By 1789, the starving French masses could no longer be controlled. Looting and riots erupted throughout Paris, ushering in the French Revolution. Rich nobles fled to the countryside, leaving behind their highly skilled chefs and the fine wines from their cellars. Suddenly, unemployed cooks found their way to the city’s eateries, and within a year, nearly 50 elegant restaurants had popped up in Paris.

The restaurant business truly came into its own during the early 1800s, after General Napoleon seized control of the country. He granted “freedom of pleasure” to all citizens, as he reasoned that people who were focused on champagne and fine food probably would not conspire against him. The number of restaurants rose quickly. By 1814, about three thousand restaurants were listed in a popular travel guide. Paris became the center of the new restaurant scene, which, to some degree, it remains today.

outline: 法國催生了餐廳，(but) 過程卻一點也不文明，(In fact) 事實上今天的餐飲業是法國大革命階級鬥爭的副產品。
(Back in the Middle Ages) 中世紀時，精緻餐飲是貴族的特權，平民只能去髒亂的路邊旅店；(But) 1760 年代巴黎商人愛上據說能恢復元氣的清湯，(hence) restaurant 一詞由此而來，1780 年代出現了幾家有名的餐廳。
(Ironically) 諷刺的是，這些餐廳流行的時候，多數法國人連麵包都買不起：數十年的嚴冬和苛稅讓餐桌空空，1789 年飢餓的群眾失控，巴黎各地暴動搶劫，法國大革命爆發。
有錢的貴族逃到鄉下，留下技術高超的廚師和酒窖裡的好酒，(Suddenly) 失業的廚師一下子湧進城裡的餐館，一年內巴黎冒出將近 50 家高級餐廳。
拿破崙掌權後，餐飲業真正發展起來：他給公民「享樂的自由」，(as) 因為他認為專注美食的人不會密謀反他；1814 年一本旅遊指南列了約三千家餐廳，巴黎成了餐廳文化的中心。

zh: 餐廳誕生在法國，過程卻一點也不文明。事實上，今天的餐飲業，是法國大革命期間階級鬥爭的副產品。

早在中世紀，精緻餐飲是貴族家庭獨享的特權，他們有自己的大廚房，也有私人廚師。一般大眾唯一能去的營業用餐處所，是路邊塵土滿布、破舊簡陋的旅店，陌生人擠在一起，吃的是不冷不熱的烤肉和醬汁太多的豆子，這些自助式的菜色都很普通。不過，大約在 1760 年代，巴黎的商人階級愛上了健康的清湯，大家認為這種湯能恢復元氣（restorative），「restaurant」（餐廳）這個字就是這樣來的。到了 1780 年代，這股巴黎的「健康飲食」熱潮，帶動了幾家有名的餐廳，客人可以坐在各自的桌子用餐，從許多菜色中挑選。
諷刺的是，這些餐廳越來越受歡迎的時候，大多數法國人卻連麵包都買不起。數十年的嚴冬和沉重的苛稅，讓一般人家的餐桌越來越空。到了 1789 年，政府再也控制不了飢餓的法國群眾。巴黎各地發生搶劫和暴動，揭開了法國大革命的序幕。有錢的貴族逃到鄉下，留下了技術高超的廚師和酒窖裡的好酒。失業的廚師一下子紛紛進了城裡的餐館，不到一年，巴黎就冒出了將近 50 家高級餐廳。
19 世紀初，拿破崙將軍掌控法國以後，餐飲業才真正蓬勃發展。他給所有公民「享樂的自由」，因為他認為，一心想著香檳和美食的人，大概不會密謀推翻他。餐廳的數量迅速增加。到了 1814 年，一本受歡迎的旅遊指南就列了大約三千家餐廳。巴黎成了這股新興餐廳風潮的中心，在某種程度上，到今天仍然是。

The restaurant business truly came into its own during the early 1800s, after General Napoleon seized control of the country.

title: 獵鷹術的歷史、訓練與文化意涵（History, Training, and Cultural Significance of Falconry）
paras: Falcons are powerful birds that may be trained to hunt in cooperation with humans. The art of training falcons as “hunting dogs of the skies” is called falconry. It was developed in the ancient Arabian Desert around 4000 B.C. In the past, falconry mainly involved hunting with falcons to supplement one’s diet. But now, it has become the favorite sport and pastime in the Arabian Peninsula.

Falconry includes three major processes: acquiring the falcons, training them, and hunting with them. Every year, falconers begin capturing wild falcons in June and July, the migration season. The best birds to catch are the ones with naturally nurtured hunting skills, aged one or two years. Once the falcons are captured, their heads are immediately covered with a leather hood. This is essential because they imprint as their master whomever they see first after the hood is removed. Right after a bird is caught, the training process starts. It begins by depriving the bird of food to make it easier to tame. The birds are taught to know their own name and respond to their master when called. Arab falconers live with their birds day and night in order to build a strong relationship with them.

By the end of October or mid-November, the trained falcons are ready to hunt in the desert. They have excellent vision, 2.6 times greater than that of a human. They are also the fastest divers on the planet. One hunting technique that sets them apart from other animals is that they can be trained to deliver their prey, without killing it first. This is vital in Islamic culture because animals used for food must still be alive to ensure that the meat is halal, that is, properly prepared according to Islamic law.

Falcons have played such a crucial role in traditional Islamic cultures that a number of countries in the Middle East have made them their national bird. Falconry has grown so popular that specialist hospitals have been established to take care of these magnificent birds. Falcons are even issued their own passports. They are the only animals in the United Arab Emirates that are legally allowed to travel inside planes, enjoying a level of luxury that some humans can only dream of.

outline: 訓練獵鷹和人合作狩獵的技藝稱為鷹獵，約西元前 4000 年發源於阿拉伯沙漠；(In the past) 過去是為了打獵補充食物，(But now) 現在成了阿拉伯半島最受歡迎的運動。
鷹獵包括捕鷹、訓鷹、帶鷹打獵三個過程：每年六、七月捕捉一、兩歲的野生獵鷹；(Once) 捕到後立刻蓋上皮頭罩，因為牠們會把拿掉頭罩後第一眼看到的人認作主人。
(Right after) 捉到後馬上開始訓練，先不給食物，讓牠比較容易馴服，再教牠認得自己的名字、聽到主人呼喚就回應；阿拉伯鷹獵者日夜和鷹住在一起，建立緊密的關係。
到十月底或十一月中，獵鷹就能在沙漠打獵：視力是人類的 2.6 倍，(also) 也是俯衝最快的動物；牠們能把獵物活著帶回來，這在伊斯蘭文化很重要，(that is) 因為肉要符合 halal。
獵鷹在伊斯蘭文化中地位重要，有些中東國家定為國鳥，還有專門的醫院，獵鷹 (even) 甚至有自己的護照，在阿拉伯聯合大公國是唯一能合法進入機艙的動物。

zh: 獵鷹是強壯有力的鳥，可以訓練來和人類合作打獵。把獵鷹訓練成「天空獵犬」的技藝，稱為鷹獵。鷹獵大約在西元前 4000 年發源於古代的阿拉伯沙漠。過去，鷹獵主要是帶著獵鷹打獵，用獵物補充食物；不過現在，鷹獵已經成為阿拉伯半島最受歡迎的運動和休閒活動。

鷹獵包括三個主要過程：取得獵鷹、訓練獵鷹，以及帶著獵鷹打獵。每年六月和七月是獵鷹遷徙的季節，鷹獵者在這時開始捕捉野生獵鷹。最適合捕捉的是一、兩歲，天生就有狩獵本領的獵鷹。獵鷹一捉到，就要立刻用皮製頭罩蓋住牠的頭。這一步非常重要，因為拿掉頭罩以後，獵鷹第一眼看到誰，就會把誰認作主人。獵鷹捉到以後，訓練馬上開始。第一步是先不給牠食物，讓牠比較容易馴服。接著教牠認得自己的名字，聽到主人呼喚就回應。阿拉伯的鷹獵者日夜和他們的獵鷹住在一起，和牠們建立緊密的關係。
到了十月底或十一月中，訓練好的獵鷹就可以到沙漠打獵了。獵鷹的視力極佳，是人類的 2.6 倍；牠們也是地球上俯衝速度最快的動物。獵鷹有一項狩獵本領和其他動物不同：經過訓練，牠們可以把獵物帶回來，不先殺死。這在伊斯蘭文化中非常重要，因為當作食物的動物必須還活著，才能確保肉是清真（halal）的，也就是依照伊斯蘭律法妥善處理。
獵鷹在傳統伊斯蘭文化中非常重要，好幾個中東國家都把獵鷹定為國鳥。鷹獵越來越受歡迎，甚至有專門照顧這些雄偉鳥類的醫院。獵鷹還能領到自己的護照。在阿拉伯聯合大公國，獵鷹是唯一可以合法搭飛機、待在機艙裡的動物，享受的奢華待遇，有些人只能夢想。

title: 高爾夫球的演進與凹洞的空氣動力學原理（Evolution of Golf Balls and Dimple Aerodynamics）
paras: Since golf started in the 15th century, many advances have occurred in the game, including significant changes to the golf ball. Early golf was played with a rounded wooden ball before the Featherie, a leather sack stuffed with goose or chicken feathers, became the norm. Then, in 1848, the Gutta Percha ball was introduced, which was made from the juice of the leaves of the gutta tree (a tropical tree native to Malaysia) and was considerably more durable and affordable than its predecessor. The next advancement occurred in the early 1900s with the development of the Haskell. It was the first ball featuring a center rubber core and an outer cover. The Haskell traveled up to 20 yards farther than the Gutta Percha ball and was more durable. In 1905, William Taylor introduced the first dimpled ball, a ball covered with tiny holes on the surface. By the 1930s, golf balls with rows of dimples were accepted as the standard design. Most golf balls today consist of rubber thread wound around a rubber core and coated with dimpled enamel.

Dimples play an important role in a golf ball’s performance because these markings and patterns enhance the ball’s aerodynamics. When a ball is hit and moves through the air, it experiences two major aerodynamic forces: lift and drag. Drag slows the forward motion, and lift acts in a direction vertical to it. With dimples added to the ball, the force that pulls back on the ball is minimized, allowing it to travel faster and longer. Dimples also help to force the airflow downward, which pushes the ball upward. These are the same principles of aerodynamics that airplanes use to fly. In general, golf balls with small, shallow dimples tend to have a longer, lower flight path, whereas those with deeper dimples have a higher flight path. Golfers can choose their balls based on what they need for a particular shot or for particular weather.

outline: (Since) 高爾夫球從 15 世紀出現以來進步很多，球的改變尤其大：早期用圓形木球，後來羽毛球（用皮囊塞鵝毛或雞毛）成為主流。
(Then) 1848 年出現古塔膠球，比羽毛球耐用也便宜得多；(The next advancement) 下一個進展是 1900 年代初的 Haskell 球，有橡膠核心，比古塔膠球最多可多飛 20 碼，也更耐用。
1905 年 William Taylor 推出第一顆有凹洞的球，1930 年代成排凹洞成為標準設計；現在的球多半是橡膠線纏繞橡膠核心，外面包一層有凹洞的琺瑯。
凹洞很重要，(because) 因為能改善空氣動力：凹洞把往後拉的阻力減到最小，球飛得更遠，凹洞 (also) 也把氣流往下推，讓球往上升，和飛機飛行的原理一樣。
(In general) 一般來說，小而淺的凹洞讓球飛得遠而低，(whereas) 深的凹洞則讓球飛得高，球員可以依擊球需要或天氣選球。

zh: 自從高爾夫球在 15 世紀出現以來，這項運動有了許多進步，其中包括高爾夫球本身的重大改變。早期的高爾夫球用的是圓形木球，後來羽毛球（Featherie）成了主流，這種球是在皮囊裡塞滿鵝毛或雞毛。接著在 1848 年，古塔膠球（Gutta Percha）問世，原料是古塔樹（一種原產於馬來西亞的熱帶樹木）葉子的汁液，比之前的羽毛球耐用得多，也便宜得多。下一個進展出現在 1900 年代初，也就是 Haskell 球的發明。這是第一顆有橡膠核心、外面再包一層外殼的球。Haskell 球最多可以比古塔膠球多飛 20 碼，也更耐用。1905 年，William Taylor 推出第一顆有凹洞的球，也就是表面布滿小凹洞的球。到了 1930 年代，表面有成排凹洞的高爾夫球，已經是公認的標準設計。現在的高爾夫球大多是用橡膠線纏繞橡膠核心，外面再包一層有凹洞的琺瑯。

凹洞對高爾夫球的表現非常重要，因為這些凹痕和紋路能改善球的空氣動力。球擊出以後在空中前進時，會有兩種主要的空氣動力作用在球上：升力和阻力。阻力讓球往前的速度變慢，升力的方向則和阻力垂直。球加上凹洞以後，往後拉的力量就減到最小，讓球飛得更快、更遠。凹洞也有助於把氣流往下推，讓球往上升。飛機能飛，靠的也是同樣的空氣動力原理。一般來說，凹洞小而淺的高爾夫球，飛行路徑比較遠、比較低；凹洞比較深的球，飛行路徑則比較高。球員可以依照某一桿的擊球需要或當天的天氣選球。

title: 羅傑·伊伯特影展歡迎詞（Welcome to Roger Ebert’s Film Festival）
paras: I am thrilled to welcome you to the 20th annual Roger Ebert’s Film Festival, a special event in partnership with the University of Illinois College of Media, the greater Champaign-Urbana community, and movie lovers everywhere. Little did we think, back in 1999, that our experiment in reinventing the film festival—to make a festival that celebrated overlooked films, formats and genres, and the women and men who made those films—would become a landmark annual event in the life of our community and contribute to the renovation of the remarkable Virginia Theater, our home from the very beginning.

In selecting the films for this year, Chaz Ebert and I looked to women filmmakers for our inspiration. Fully half of our films are either directed or co-directed by women, and several others have women in powerful producing roles. Films directed or co-directed by women include “13th,” directed by Ava DuVernay, “Belle,” directed by Amma Asante, and “American Splendor,” directed by Shari Springer Berman and Robert Pulcini. And women producers include Lynda Obst and Emma Thomas (“Interstellar”) and Ruth Ann Harnisch and Danielle Renfrew Behrens (“Columbus”).

Our opening night film is “The Fugitive,” directed by University of Illinois alumnus Andrew Davis. Our Saturday night film is the classic “The Big Lebowski.” Our guest will be the Hollywood legend Jeff Dowd. And of course The Alloy Orchestra will be back, this year with “A Page of Madness,” the classic Japanese silent film.

We would like to thank our sponsors, volunteers, festival pass holders, and individual ticket holders for their welcome participation in this endeavor. We look forward to your unwavering support as our festival continues to blossom each spring in central Illinois. We especially want to thank the University of Illinois for their loyal support year after year.
This festival is Roger Ebert’s gift to his hometown, and for that we thank him and his wife Chaz. They continue to be a remarkable team, and it is an honor to work with them.

今年選片的時候，Chaz Ebert 和我以女性電影人作為靈感來源。整整一半的影片由女性執導或共同執導，另外還有好幾部片子由女性擔任重要的製片。由女性執導或共同執導的影片，包括 Ava DuVernay 執導的《13th》、Amma Asante 執導的《Belle》，以及 Shari Springer Berman 和 Robert Pulcini 共同執導的《American Splendor》。女性製片則有《Interstellar》的 Lynda Obst 和 Emma Thomas，以及《Columbus》的 Ruth Ann Harnisch 和 Danielle Renfrew Behrens。
開幕片是伊利諾大學校友 Andrew Davis 執導的《The Fugitive》。星期六晚上放映的是經典電影《The Big Lebowski》。我們的嘉賓是好萊塢傳奇人物 Jeff Dowd。當然，Alloy 管弦樂團今年也會回來，帶來的是日本經典默片《A Page of Madness》。

title: 風暴追逐的興起與安全問題（The Rise and Safety Issues of Storm Chasing）
paras: Storm chasing is broadly defined as the pursuit of any severe weather condition, for reasons ranging from curiosity, adventure, and scientific exploration to media coverage.

Chasing often involves driving thousands of miles in order to witness a relatively short window of time of severe weather. It is not uncommon for a storm chaser to end up empty-handed on any particular day. Most storm chasers are not professional meteorologists, and many chasers devote significant time and effort to learning meteorology, the study of the atmosphere, and the weather forming process. The amount of equipment used for storm chasing also varies. Some prefer a minimalist approach where only basic photographic equipment is taken on a chase, while others use everything from satellite-based tracking systems and live data feeds to vehicle-mounted weather stations and hail guards.

There are inherent dangers involved in pursuing hazardous weather. These range from lightning and tornadoes to unsafe road conditions and reduced visibility from heavy rain. In some situations, a severe downburst airstream can happen unexpectedly and push automobiles around. Tornadoes affect a relatively small area and are predictable enough to be avoided if a safe distance is maintained. Lightning, however, is an unavoidable hazard. “Core punching,” which is storm chasers’ slang for driving through the part of a thunderstorm that has the heaviest rain to collect critical information, is recognized as extremely hazardous.

Today, interest in storm chasing has surged. Amateurs and YouTube fame seekers with video cameras now race with professionals to see who can get the closest and most dramatic images of churning storms, and this is causing a growing safety threat. A group of storm-chase veterans has advocated the adoption of a code of ethics emphasizing safety, courtesy, and objectivity. However, many chasers oppose self-policing, as is often the case with people involved in other dangerous leisure activities.

outline: 追風暴廣義是指追逐各種惡劣天氣，原因從好奇、冒險、科學探索到媒體報導都有。
追風暴常要開幾千英里，只為看短短一段惡劣天氣，空手而回也很常見；多數追風者不是專業氣象學家，很多人花大量時間學習氣象學。
使用的裝備 (also) 也各不相同：有人只帶基本攝影器材，(while) 有人從衛星追蹤系統、即時資料到車載氣象站、防冰雹罩一應俱全。
追逐危險天氣本身就危險：閃電、龍捲風、路況不佳、大雨遮蔽視線都是威脅；龍捲風保持距離就能避開，閃電 (however) 卻無法避免，穿越雷暴中心的「core punching」更是極度危險。
(Today) 如今追風暴越來越熱門，業餘玩家和專業人士搶拍最震撼的畫面，安全威脅越來越大；資深追風者提倡倫理守則，(However) 不過許多追風者反對自律規範。

zh: 追風暴（storm chasing）廣義來說，是指追逐任何惡劣的天氣，原因從好奇、冒險、科學探索到媒體報導都有。
追風暴常常要開好幾千英里的車，只為了親眼看到時間相對短暫的惡劣天氣。追風暴的人在某一天空手而回，並不少見。大部分追風暴的人都不是專業的氣象學家，很多人花了大量的時間和心力，學習氣象學，也就是研究大氣和天氣形成過程的學問。追風暴用的裝備多寡也各不相同。有些人喜歡極簡，追風暴時只帶基本的攝影器材；也有人從衛星追蹤系統、即時資料傳輸，到車上的氣象站和防冰雹罩，什麼都用上。
追逐危險的天氣，本身就有危險。這些危險從閃電、龍捲風，到不安全的路況、大雨造成的能見度降低都有。有時候，強烈的下爆氣流會突然出現，把汽車推來推去。龍捲風影響的範圍相對小，也相當可以預測，只要保持安全距離，就能避開。不過，閃電是避不開的危險。「core punching」是追風暴者的行話，指開車穿過雷雨中雨勢最大的區域，蒐集關鍵資料，大家公認這種做法極度危險。
如今，追風暴的熱潮急速升溫。帶著攝影機的業餘玩家和想在 YouTube 成名的人，現在和專業人士競爭，看誰能拍到最近、最震撼的翻騰風暴畫面，這帶來越來越大的安全威脅。一群資深的追風暴者提倡採用一套倫理守則，強調安全、禮貌和客觀。然而，許多追風暴者反對自我約束的規範，參與其他危險休閒活動的人，往往也是這樣。

title: 育空路標森林的起源與特色（Origin and Characteristics of Yukon's Signpost Forest）
paras: Deep within the Yukon, one of the most densely wooded areas of Canada, sits a patch of land that is unlike any other forest on the planet. Instead of a canopy of treetops spreading across the horizon, tens of thousands of signposts perch haphazardly one on top of the other. They are all part of the Signpost Forest, the largest collection of signs from places around the world. At last count, the Signpost Forest in Watson Lake, located about 10 miles north of the U.S.-Canadian border, contains 91,000 signs from spots near and far, including Berlin, Moscow, Dublin, and Hawaii.

The tradition began during the Alaska Highway Project in 1942, when U.S. soldier Carl K. Lindley spent time in Watson Lake recovering from an injury. A commanding officer asked him to repair and erect the directional signposts, and while completing the job, the homesick soldier added a sign that indicated the direction and mileage to his hometown: “Danville, Illinois, 2,835 miles.” Others followed suit, and the trend caught on. Each year, an average of 1,000 new signs are being added to the collection. Lindley’s original sign has since been lost to time. Fifty years later, in 1992, Lindley and his wife Elinor made the pilgrimage back to Watson Lake to place a replica, which is still there.

The Signpost Forest takes up a couple of acres, with huge panels snaking through the trees. There are street signs, welcome signs, signatures on dinner plates, and license plates from around the world. There are also a lot of familial signs; for example, a grandfather will put up a sign and then years later family will come back and try to find it. A lot of these are personal signs to literally say that they are here. Though the visitor center has wood and paints on hand to help create a sign, many people opt to bring their own signs, though illegally, by snatching a metal sign from their hometown and nailing it to one of the wood posts. The forest has grown so vast that the visitor center no longer tries to keep a detailed list of the signs.

outline: 加拿大育空地區的 Watson Lake 有一片特別的森林，(Instead of) 放眼望去不是樹冠，而是數萬個雜亂堆疊的路標，這就是「路標森林」，最近一次統計有 91,000 個。
這個傳統始於 1942 年阿拉斯加公路工程：美國士兵 Carl K. Lindley 在 Watson Lake 養傷時奉命修理路標，想家的他順手加了一塊指向家鄉的牌子。
其他人跟著做，每年平均新增 1,000 塊；Lindley 原來的牌子已經遺失，(Fifty years later) 五十年後的 1992 年，他和妻子重回 Watson Lake 放了一塊複製品。
路標森林占地數英畝，巨大的板子在樹林間蜿蜒，有路牌、歡迎牌、簽名餐盤和世界各地的車牌，也有很多家族牌子，(for example) 例如祖父立了一塊，多年後家人回來找。
(Though) 雖然遊客中心備有木板和顏料，很多人還是選擇自己帶牌子，從家鄉拔下金屬路牌釘在木柱上，(though) 儘管這樣做不合法；森林已經大到遊客中心不再詳細記錄每塊牌子。

zh: 育空地區是加拿大林木最茂密的地區之一，在育空深處，有一片和地球上其他森林都不一樣的土地。放眼望去，看到的不是一片延伸到地平線的樹冠，而是好幾萬個雜亂地一個疊著一個的路標。這些路標都屬於「路標森林」，這裡是全世界蒐集各地路標最多的地方。根據最近一次的統計，位在美加邊界以北約 10 英里處、Watson Lake 的路標森林，共有 91,000 塊來自遠近各地的牌子，包括柏林、莫斯科、都柏林和夏威夷。

這個傳統始於 1942 年的阿拉斯加公路工程。當時，美國士兵 Carl K. Lindley 在 Watson Lake 養傷，一位指揮官要他修理、豎立指示方向的路標。想家的 Lindley 在完成工作的時候，加上了一塊牌子，標出家鄉的方向和里程：「伊利諾州丹維爾，2,835 英里」。其他人也跟著這樣做，這股風氣就流行起來。每年平均有 1,000 塊新的牌子加進來。Lindley 原來的那塊牌子，隨著時間過去，已經遺失了。五十年後的 1992 年，Lindley 和妻子 Elinor 專程回到 Watson Lake，放上一塊複製品，這塊複製品到現在還在那裡。

路標森林占地好幾英畝，一片片巨大的板子在樹林間蜿蜒。這裡有路牌、歡迎牌、簽了名的餐盤，還有來自世界各地的車牌。也有很多家族的牌子，例如祖父立了一塊牌子，多年以後，家人回來想找到它。這些牌子很多是私人的，就是要告訴大家「我們來過這裡」。雖然遊客中心備有木板和顏料，可以幫忙做牌子，很多人還是選擇自己帶牌子來，有些人甚至違法從家鄉拔下金屬路牌，釘在其中一根木柱上。這片森林已經大到遊客中心不再試著詳細記錄每一塊牌子。

The tradition began during the Alaska Highway Project in 1942, when U.S. soldier Carl K. Lindley spent time in Watson Lake recovering from an injury.

title: 匯率的歷史演變與體系（The Historical Evolution and Systems of Exchange Rates）
paras: In finance, an exchange rate is the rate at which one country’s currency is exchanged for the currency of another. The rate is set according to the respective values of the currencies to be exchanged. Before World War I, most currencies were evaluated by the Gold Standard. That is, paper currency issued by a government represented a real amount of gold held by that government. For example, in the 1930s, the British government owned about 8 times as much gold as the U.S. government. Therefore, 1 ounce of gold was worth 4.24 GBP (United Kingdom pound sterling) or 35 USD (U.S. dollars). The difference in the price of gold became the exchange rate for the two currencies: 1GBP was worth 8.25 USD.

The Gold Standard started to break down during the Second World War, when European powers printed more money than they had in gold reserves in order to fund military projects. After World War II, the Bretton Woods System was established. The U.S. dollar was chosen as the international reserve currency for trading. Every country knew how much gold a USD was worth, and thus they based the value of their currencies on the USD. All countries were expected to maintain a fixed exchange rate, but were permitted to change it in extraordinary times, such as a recession or inflation.

Unfortunately, this system could not keep pace with the fast-changing global economy. As the U.S. increased its military spending, foreign aid, and international investment in the 1960s, it no longer held gold reserves necessary to cover the volume of USD circulation around the world. Other major currencies thus became more valuable and stable compared to the USD, and the Bretton Woods System was finally abolished in 1971.

In 1976, the Jamaica Agreement formalized the floating exchange rate system that continues to this day. The value of a country’s currency may vary according to the supply and demand of the foreign exchange market. Countries around the world can also allow their central banks to determine their own exchange rate.

outline: 匯率是一國貨幣兌換另一國貨幣的比率，依兩種貨幣各自的價值決定。
(Before World War I) 第一次世界大戰前，多數貨幣採金本位，(That is) 也就是紙幣代表政府持有的黃金；(For example) 例如一盎司黃金值 4.24 英鎊或 35 美元，(Therefore) 所以一英鎊值 8.25 美元。
二戰期間歐洲列強印出超過黃金儲備的鈔票，金本位開始瓦解；(After World War II) 二戰後建立布列敦森林體系，各國依美元訂定幣值，維持固定匯率。
(Unfortunately) 可惜這個體系跟不上全球經濟：1960 年代美國的黃金儲備不足以支應全球流通的美元，其他主要貨幣 (thus) 因此比美元更穩定，布列敦森林體系終於在 1971 年廢除。
(In 1976) 1976 年牙買加協定確立了沿用至今的浮動匯率制度，一國貨幣的價值隨外匯市場的供需變動，各國也可以讓中央銀行決定自己的匯率。

zh: 在金融上，匯率是一國貨幣兌換另一國貨幣的比率。匯率依照要兌換的兩種貨幣各自的價值來決定。第一次世界大戰以前，大多數貨幣的價值都以金本位評定。也就是說，政府發行的紙幣，代表政府實際持有的一定數量的黃金。例如在 1930 年代，英國政府擁有的黃金大約是美國政府的 8 倍。因此，1 盎司黃金值 4.24 英鎊（GBP），或 35 美元（USD）。黃金價格的差異，就成了這兩種貨幣的匯率：1 英鎊值 8.25 美元。
第二次世界大戰期間，歐洲列強為了支應軍事計畫，印出超過黃金儲備的鈔票，金本位開始瓦解。二戰以後，布列敦森林體系建立。美元獲選為國際貿易的儲備貨幣。每個國家都知道一美元值多少黃金，因此各國都以美元作為訂定本國貨幣價值的基準。所有國家原則上都要維持固定匯率，但遇到經濟衰退或通貨膨脹等特殊時期，可以調整匯率。
可惜的是，這個體系跟不上快速變化的全球經濟。1960 年代，美國增加軍事支出、對外援助和國際投資，持有的黃金儲備已經不足以支應全世界流通的美元數量。因此，其他主要貨幣和美元相比，變得更有價值、也更穩定，布列敦森林體系終於在 1971 年廢除。
1976 年，牙買加協定正式確立了沿用至今的浮動匯率制度。一國貨幣的價值，可能隨外匯市場的供需而變動。世界各國也可以讓中央銀行決定自己的匯率。

title: 現代廢水處理流程（Modern Wastewater Treatment Process）
paras: Early civilizations often built drainage systems in urban areas to handle rainwater that ran down the street during a storm. The Romans constructed elaborate systems that also drained wastewater from the public baths. However, as the population of the cities grew, the old drainage systems became overloaded. During the Industrial Revolution, manufacturing waste was added to sewage, which increased the need for more efficient sewage treatment. In the mid-19th century, the first steps were taken to treat wastewater.

Sewage or wastewater treatment in modern times is the process of removing harmful physical, chemical, and biological elements from wastewater and house sewage. The whole process starts with screening out large objects such as paper and wood, and removing heavy materials like dirt. The screened wastewater is then ready to go through a series of concrete tanks for further treatment. In the second step, the sewage passes into the primary tanks. Here, human waste, called sludge, settles to the bottom while oils and grease float to the top, where they are collected. At the same time, organic matter like eggshells or coffee grounds in the sewage is broken down into smaller substances. The remaining sewage then enters the secondary tanks for the third stage of treatment. The solids that were not treated in the primary tanks are removed here through decomposition, which digests the material. Then, the liquid sewage is filtered through sand. This filtering process gets rid of almost all bacteria, as well as other solid particles that remain in the water. Finally, the wastewater flows into the last tanks, where the chemical chlorine is added to kill the remaining bacteria. After the bacteria are destroyed, the chlorine is eliminated from the water, and the treated clean water is discharged into a river or the ocean.

outline: 早期文明就建排水系統處理雨水，(However) 然而城市人口增加，舊系統不堪負荷，工業革命時製造業廢棄物又混進汙水，19 世紀中期開始處理廢水。
現代汙水處理是把廢水和家庭汙水中有害的物理、化學、生物成分去除：第一步先篩掉紙、木頭等大型物品，去除泥土等重物，接著汙水進入一連串混凝土池。
(In the second step) 第二步，汙水進入初級池，人類排泄物（汙泥）沉到底部，油脂浮到上面收集起來，(At the same time) 同時蛋殼、咖啡渣等有機物分解成較小的物質。
剩下的汙水進入二級池做第三階段處理，初級池沒處理到的固體在這裡分解去除；(Then) 接著液態汙水用沙過濾，去除幾乎所有細菌和殘留的固體微粒。
(Finally) 最後廢水流進最後的池子，加氯殺死剩下的細菌，細菌消滅以後再除去水中的氯，處理乾淨的水排進河川或海洋。

zh: 早期的文明常在都市地區興建排水系統，處理暴風雨時順著街道流下的雨水。羅馬人建造了精密的排水系統，也排放公共浴場的廢水。然而，隨著城市人口增加，舊的排水系統變得不堪負荷。工業革命時期，製造業的廢棄物加進了汙水，處理汙水更需要有效率的方法。到了 19 世紀中期，人類開始踏出處理廢水的第一步。

現代的汙水（廢水）處理，是把廢水和家庭汙水中有害的物理、化學和生物成分去除的過程。整個過程從篩除紙張、木頭等大型物品開始，同時去除泥土等重物。篩過的廢水接著要流經一連串的混凝土池，做進一步的處理。第二步，汙水流進初級池。在這裡，人類的排泄物，也就是所謂的汙泥，沉到池底，油和油脂則浮到上面，收集起來。同時，汙水裡蛋殼、咖啡渣等有機物，會分解成比較小的物質。剩下的汙水接著進入二級池，做第三階段的處理。初級池沒有處理到的固體，在這裡經過分解，消化掉。然後，液態汙水用沙過濾。這道過濾程序可以去除幾乎所有的細菌，以及水中殘留的其他固體微粒。最後，廢水流進最後的池子，加入氯這種化學物質，殺死剩下的細菌。細菌消滅以後，再把水中的氯除去，處理乾淨的水就排進河川或海洋。

ms.t: Sewage or wastewater treatment in modern times is the process of removing harmful physical, chemical, and biological elements from wastewater and house sewage.

title: 馬里亞納海溝的深海汙染（Deep-Sea Pollution in Mariana Trench）
paras: The planet’s deepest point is in the Pacific Ocean’s Mariana Trench, which lies miles below the sea surface. According to a new study published in Nature Ecology & Evolution, even in this remote locale, creatures cannot escape pollution.

A team of researchers recently sent a remotely operated vehicle into the depths of the Mariana Trench. They found that extraordinarily high levels of forbidden industrial chemicals are contaminating marine life more than 7 miles deep in the trench. The small hard-shelled marine life that the robotic submarine brought to the surface was polluted with toxic chemicals, with toxin levels 50 times greater than those of the most heavily polluted rivers in the world.

These pollution levels were not the only alarming aspect of the discovery. The types of compounds found were all considered “persistent organic pollutants” (POPs), meaning they stick around in the environment for a very long time. Two of the most prevalent types are PCBs and PBDEs. PCBs were once used in many industrial applications, but were outlawed in the United States in the 1970s after being linked to cancer. Similarly, PBDEs were used in a wide range of products—from electronics to couch cushions. Neither chemical breaks down in the environment.

These compounds stick to the surface of materials like plastic. Many creatures mistakenly eat this colorful but toxic material, causing the POPs to build up in their bodies, lurking in their fat tissues. When these sea creatures die, their POP-riddled bodies sink to the ocean floor, where deep-sea marine life eat their remains. POPs are therefore transferred to other creatures along the food chain.
The Mariana Trench is many miles away from any industrial source. This suggests that these pollutants travel over long distances despite having been prohibited worldwide decades ago.

outline: 地球最深處在太平洋的馬里亞納海溝，《Nature Ecology & Evolution》的新研究發現，即使在這麼偏遠的地方，生物也逃不過汙染。
研究團隊派遙控載具潛入海溝，發現海溝 7 英里以下的海洋生物體內，禁用的工業化學物質濃度高得驚人，帶上來的小型甲殼生物毒素濃度是全世界汙染最嚴重河川的 50 倍。
這些化合物屬於「持久性有機汙染物」(POPs)，最常見的是 PCBs 和 PBDEs：PCBs 曾廣泛用於工業，1970 年代因為和癌症有關而禁用；(Similarly) PBDEs 同樣用途廣泛，從電子產品到沙發坐墊都有；兩種都不會在環境中分解。
這些化合物附著在塑膠上，生物誤吃後在體內脂肪累積；生物死後沉到海底，深海生物吃下遺骸，POPs (therefore) 因此沿著食物鏈傳下去。
馬里亞納海溝離任何工業汙染源都很遠，表示這些汙染物 (despite) 雖然幾十年前就全球禁用，仍能長距離移動。

zh: 地球最深的地方，在太平洋的馬里亞納海溝，位於海面下好幾英里。根據《Nature Ecology & Evolution》期刊最新發表的一項研究，即使在這麼偏遠的地方，生物也逃不過汙染。
一個研究團隊最近派了一具遙控載具潛入馬里亞納海溝深處。他們發現，在海溝 7 英里以下的深處，濃度極高的禁用工業化學物質正在汙染海洋生物。這艘機器潛水艇帶回海面的小型甲殼類海洋生物，體內有有毒的化學物質，毒素濃度是全世界汙染最嚴重的河川的 50 倍。
令人憂心的，不只是這些汙染程度。研究找到的化合物，全都屬於「持久性有機汙染物」（POPs），意思是這些物質會在環境中留存很長的時間。最常見的兩種是 PCBs 和 PBDEs。PCBs 過去用在許多工業用途上，但在 1970 年代發現和癌症有關以後，美國就禁用了。同樣地，PBDEs 也曾用在各式各樣的產品上，從電子產品到沙發坐墊都有。這兩種化學物質都不會在環境中分解。
這些化合物會附著在塑膠等材料的表面。很多生物誤吃了這些色彩鮮豔卻有毒的東西，POPs 就在牠們體內累積，潛藏在脂肪組織裡。這些海洋生物死後，充滿 POPs 的屍體沉到海底，深海的海洋生物再吃下這些遺骸。POPs 就這樣沿著食物鏈，傳到其他生物身上。
馬里亞納海溝離任何工業汙染源都有好幾英里遠。這表示，雖然這些汙染物幾十年前就已經在全球禁用，仍然能夠遠距離移動。

They found that extraordinarily high levels of forbidden industrial chemicals are contaminating marine life more than 7 miles deep in the trench.
The types of compounds found were all considered “persistent organic pollutants” (POPs), meaning they stick around in the environment for a very long time.
POPs are therefore transferred to other creatures along the food chain.
This suggests that these pollutants travel over long distances despite having been prohibited worldwide decades ago.

title: 紐西蘭全黑隊與毛利哈卡舞（New Zealand’s All Blacks and the Māori Haka）
paras: The All Blacks, New Zealand’s national rugby team, is widely credited for bringing the “haka” to the world stage. Immediately before kick-off, the whole team will issue a warlike chant, stamping their feet, slapping their thighs, rolling their eyes, flicking their tongues, and making aggressive gestures in unison. This performance before each match, which is intended to heighten their morale and intimidate opponents, is a sight to behold. No other international sporting team possesses a pre-match ritual as powerful as the famed All Blacks haka.

What does “haka” mean? Haka is often thought of as a broad term for Māori war dances traditionally used to intimidate the enemy and prepare the warriors for battle. Most people believe it was performed either on the battlefield prior to engaging the enemy, or as the warriors were leaving their own village en route to a battle. But in the language of Māori, the word haka simply means a dance. The dance is accompanied by a chant that expresses emotions or tells ancient stories. While many haka should be performed by males, there are some haka that can be performed by anyone, male or female. There are even some women-only haka.

Thanks to the All Blacks, two of the haka have become widely renowned: Ka Mate and Kapa o Pango. The former was composed by a Māori chief in the early 1800s about how he outsmarted his enemies. It was first performed by the All Blacks in 1906. The latter was written specifically for the team in 2005. They are now performed interchangeably by the All Blacks.

Today, different varieties of haka are performed on various ceremonial occasions—from receiving distinguished guests to birthdays, weddings, or the funerals of chiefs and people of high status. Though the practice had traditionally been limited to Māori communities, it has now spread far beyond that. Māori and New Zealanders of European heritage alike view doing the haka with a sense of pride, both on the rugby field and outside it. The haka has become the most recognizable symbol of New Zealanders as a people.

outline: 紐西蘭國家橄欖球隊全黑隊讓哈卡舞登上世界舞台：開球前全隊齊聲吼出戰歌，跺腳、瞪眼、吐舌，用來提振士氣、震懾對手。
一般認為哈卡是毛利戰舞的統稱，戰士出征或在戰場上表演，用來威嚇敵人、做好作戰準備，(But) 但在毛利語中 haka 只是「舞蹈」的意思，搭配表達情感或講述古老故事的吟唱。
(While) 雖然許多哈卡應該由男性表演，也有男女都能跳的哈卡，甚至有只限女性的哈卡。
(Thanks to) 因為全黑隊，兩支哈卡廣為人知：(The former) Ka Mate 是一位毛利酋長在 1800 年代初所作，1906 年全黑隊首次表演；(The latter) Kapa o Pango 是 2005 年專為球隊寫的。
如今哈卡在迎賓、生日、婚禮、酋長和地位崇高者的葬禮等儀式場合表演，(Though) 雖然傳統上只在毛利社群，現在已經普及，毛利人和歐洲裔紐西蘭人都以跳哈卡為榮，哈卡成了紐西蘭人最具代表性的象徵。

zh: 全黑隊（All Blacks）是紐西蘭國家橄欖球隊，一般公認，是他們把「哈卡」（haka）帶上了世界舞台。比賽一開球之前，全隊會齊聲喊出好戰的吟唱，一面跺腳、拍打大腿、轉動眼珠、吐舌頭，一面做出各種威嚇的動作，動作整齊劃一。這是全黑隊每場比賽前的表演，目的是提振自己的士氣、震懾對手，場面十分壯觀。沒有其他國際運動隊伍的賽前儀式，像著名的全黑隊哈卡舞這麼有氣勢。
「哈卡」是什麼意思？一般人常把哈卡當作毛利戰舞的統稱，傳統上用來威嚇敵人，讓戰士做好作戰的準備。大多數人認為，哈卡是在戰場上和敵人交戰之前，或是戰士離開自己的村落、前往戰場的途中表演的。不過，在毛利語中，haka 這個字只是「舞蹈」的意思。跳舞的時候會搭配吟唱，用來表達情感或講述古老的故事。雖然很多哈卡應該由男性表演，也有一些哈卡不分男女，誰都可以跳，甚至還有一些只限女性的哈卡。
因為全黑隊的關係，有兩支哈卡變得廣為人知：Ka Mate 和 Kapa o Pango。前者是一位毛利酋長在 1800 年代初創作的，內容是他怎麼智取敵人，全黑隊在 1906 年第一次表演這支哈卡。後者是 2005 年專門替全黑隊寫的。現在全黑隊兩支都會表演，交替使用。
現在，各種不同的哈卡在許多典禮場合表演，從迎接貴賓到生日、婚禮，或是酋長和地位崇高的人的葬禮都有。表演哈卡傳統上只限於毛利社群，現在卻已經普及到毛利社群以外。不論是毛利人，還是歐洲裔的紐西蘭人，都以跳哈卡為榮，在橄欖球場上是這樣，在球場外也是。哈卡已經成為紐西蘭人最具代表性的象徵。

title: 美國聯邦教育法案 ESSA 與評估改革（US Federal Education Act ESSA and Assessment Reform）
paras: In 2015, President Obama of the USA signed the Every Student Succeeds Act (ESSA), replacing the Bush-era No Child Left Behind (NCLB) that had been in effect since 2001. This new Act provides states with more decision-making power regarding curriculum, instruction, and assessment. Below are some big-picture ideas influencing many states as they approach the assessment task.

One important idea is flexibility. For years, states have used standardized K-12 assessments, similar to the SAT and ACT for college application, to measure student achievement. They are easy to use, but they fail to give a complete picture of how a student is progressing. Thus, states are rethinking one-size-fits-all standardized assessments and are instead considering personalized, student-centered assessments in schools. Obviously, the task is difficult and time-consuming. Fortunately, modern technology can help solve this dilemma. For instance, computer adaptive assessments can automatically adjust questions based on a student’s performances on the previous questions. This mechanism prevents the computer from giving questions that are obviously too easy or too difficult for the student. It thus allows teachers to quickly assess a student’s level of understanding and provide instant feedback to help in the learning process.

Another idea is multi-subject testing. Several states have started to incorporate subjects beyond the traditional math and reading items in their K-12 assessments. All 50 states include tests on science at least twice prior to senior high school, and some are now starting to include social studies, government, or economics. Some states are also moving toward assessing multiple subjects on one test, for example, reading and social studies.

A third idea is the emphasis on students’ learning process. In pursuit of a student-centered approach, many states are putting more emphasis on assessments throughout the learning process rather than on traditional end-of-year summative tests. Teachers are encouraged to accumulate data at different points in their students’ learning process. These data together present a more complete picture of a student’s learning.

The last idea regards the purpose of assessment. Assessment should be used to inform both teachers’ instruction and students’ learning. Teachers can modify their teaching based on students’ performance on tests; students can identify their own problems and make plans for improvement.

outline: 2015 年歐巴馬總統簽署《每個學生都成功法》(ESSA)，取代 2001 年起實施的《有教無類法》(NCLB)，讓各州在課程、教學和評量上有更多決定權，以下是許多州規劃評量時參考的大方向。
(One important idea) 第一是彈性：標準化測驗無法完整呈現學習進展，(Thus) 所以各州改考慮以學生為中心的評量；(Fortunately) 幸好科技可以幫忙，(For instance) 例如電腦適性測驗會依學生前面的作答調整題目。
(Another idea) 第二是多科目測驗：有些州在數學和閱讀之外加考自然、社會、公民或經濟，也有州在一份測驗裡同時評量多個科目。
(A third idea) 第三是重視學習過程：為了以學生為中心，許多州更重視學習過程中的評量，不只看學年末的總結性測驗，也鼓勵老師在不同時間點蒐集資料，拼出學生學習的完整樣貌。
(The last idea) 最後是評量的目的：評量應該同時引導老師的教學和學生的學習，老師依學生表現調整教學，學生找出自己的問題、擬定改進計畫。

zh: 2015 年，美國總統歐巴馬簽署了《每個學生都成功法》（ESSA），取代小布希時代從 2001 年起實施的《有教無類法》（NCLB）。這項新法讓各州在課程、教學和評量上，有更多的決定權。以下是影響許多州規劃評量工作的幾個大方向。

一個重要的方向是彈性。多年來，各州都用從幼稚園到 12 年級（K-12）的標準化評量來測量學生的學習成就，就像申請大學用的 SAT 和 ACT 一樣。這些評量容易使用，卻無法完整呈現學生的學習進展。因此，各州正在重新思考這種一體適用的標準化評量，改為考慮在學校採用個人化、以學生為中心的評量。顯然，這項工作既困難又費時。幸好，現代科技可以幫忙解決這個難題。例如，電腦適性測驗可以依照學生前面幾題的表現，自動調整題目。這套機制能避免電腦出明顯太簡單或太難的題目給學生，讓老師很快就能評估學生理解的程度，立即給予回饋，幫助學生學習。
另一個方向是多科目測驗。有幾個州已經開始在 K-12 評量中，加入傳統的數學和閱讀以外的科目。全部 50 個州在高中以前，都至少考兩次自然科學，有些州現在也開始加考社會、公民或經濟。有些州還朝著在一份測驗裡同時評量多個科目發展，例如閱讀加上社會。
第三個方向是重視學生的學習過程。為了以學生為中心，許多州更重視學習過程中的評量，而不是傳統的學年末總結性測驗。這些州也鼓勵老師在學生學習過程的不同時間點累積資料。這些資料合在一起，可以更完整地呈現學生的學習情形。
最後一個方向和評量的目的有關。評量應該同時用來引導老師的教學和學生的學習。老師可以依照學生在測驗中的表現調整教學；學生可以找出自己的問題，擬定改進的計畫。

title: 印尼天貝：從傳統食物到世界之寶（Indonesian Tempeh: From Traditional Food to World Treasure）
paras: Tempeh (or tempe), a traditional soy product from Indonesia, is hailed as the country’s “gift to the world,” like kimchi from Korea or miso from Japan.

A stable, cheap source of protein in Indonesia for centuries, tempeh is a fermented food originating from the island of Java. It was discovered during tofu production when discarded soybean residue caught microbial spores from the air and grew certain whitish fungi around it. When this fermented residue was found to be edible and tasty, people began producing it at home for daily consumption across the country. This has given rise to many variations in its flavor and texture throughout different Indonesian regions.

Tempeh is high in protein and low in fat, and contains a host of vitamins. In fact, it is the only reported plant-based source of vitamin B12. Apart from being able to help reduce cholesterol, increase bone density, and promote muscle recovery, tempeh has a lot of polyphenols that protect skin cells and slow down the aging process. Best of all, with the same protein quality as meat and the ability to take on many flavors and textures, tempeh is a great meat substitute—something the vegetarian and vegan communities have been quick in adopting.

In addition to its highly nutritional makeup, tempeh has diverse preparation possibilities. It can be served as a main course (usually in curries) or a side dish to be eaten with rice, as a deep-fried snack, or even blended into smoothies and healthy juices. Though not yet a popular food among international diners, you may find tempeh-substituted BLTs (bacon, lettuce, tomato sandwiches) in San Francisco as easily as you can find vegetarian burgers with tempeh patties in Bali.

For the people of Indonesia, tempeh is not just food but also has cultural value. With the Indonesian traditional fabric batik being recognized by UNESCO as “Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity,” tempeh has great potential for this honor as well.

outline: 天貝是印尼傳統黃豆製品，和韓國泡菜、日本味噌一樣，稱為這個國家「給世界的禮物」。
天貝源自爪哇島，幾百年來是印尼穩定又便宜的蛋白質來源：做豆腐丟掉的豆渣沾上空氣中的孢子，長出白色菌絲，(When) 人們發現這種發酵豆渣好吃，就開始在家做，各地也發展出不同風味。
天貝高蛋白、低脂肪，(In fact) 是唯一有紀錄的植物性維生素 B12 來源；(Apart from) 除了有益健康，(Best of all) 最棒的是蛋白質品質和肉一樣，又能吸收各種風味，素食者很快就接受了。
(In addition to) 天貝的吃法也很多：主菜、配菜、炸成點心，甚至打成果昔；(Though) 雖然國際上還不普遍，舊金山已經吃得到天貝 BLT 三明治，峇里島也有天貝漢堡排。
對印尼人來說，天貝 (not just … but also) 不只是食物，也有文化價值；印尼蠟染已經登錄聯合國教科文組織「人類非物質文化遺產」，天貝也很有機會獲得這項榮譽。

zh: 天貝（tempeh，也拼作 tempe）是印尼傳統的大豆製品，就像韓國的泡菜、日本的味噌一樣，素有印尼「送給世界的禮物」之稱。
幾百年來，天貝一直是印尼穩定又便宜的蛋白質來源，這種發酵食品源自爪哇島。天貝是在製作豆腐時發現的：丟棄的豆渣沾上空氣中的微生物孢子，周圍長出一層白色的真菌。後來人們發現這種發酵過的豆渣可以吃，而且很美味，全國各地就開始在家自己做，天天吃。印尼各地因此發展出許多風味和口感不同的天貝。
天貝蛋白質高、脂肪低，還含有多種維生素；事實上，天貝是目前唯一已知含維生素 B12 的植物性食物。天貝除了有助於降低膽固醇、增加骨質密度、促進肌肉恢復，還含有大量的多酚，可以保護皮膚細胞、延緩老化。最棒的是，天貝的蛋白質品質和肉一樣好，又能做出各種風味和口感，是很好的肉類替代品，素食者和純素食者很快就接受了。
天貝不但營養豐富，料理方式也很多元。可以當主菜（通常做成咖哩）或配飯的小菜，可以炸成點心，甚至可以打進果昔和健康果汁裡。雖然天貝在國際上還不算熱門的食物，但你在舊金山可以輕易找到用天貝取代培根的 BLT（培根、生菜、番茄三明治），就像在峇里島可以輕易找到天貝肉排做的素食漢堡一樣。
對印尼人來說，天貝不只是食物，也有文化價值。印尼的傳統布料蠟染已經列入聯合國教科文組織的「人類非物質文化遺產」，天貝也很有希望獲得這項殊榮。

title: 催眠的科學與應用（The Science and Application of Hypnosis）
paras: When Dr. David Spiegel emerged from a three-hour shoulder surgery in 1972, he didn’t use any pain medication to recover. Instead, he hypnotized himself. It worked—to the surprise of everyone but Spiegel himself, who has studied hypnosis for 45 years.

Hypnosis is often misunderstood as a sleep-like state in which a person is put to sleep and does whatever he is asked to do. But according to Dr. Spiegel, it is a state of highly focused attention and intense concentration. Being hypnotized, you tune out most of the stimuli around you. You focus intently on the subject at hand, to the near exclusion of any other thought. This trance-like state can be an effective tool to control pain, ease anxiety, and deal with stress.

Not all people, however, are equally hypnotizable. In a recent study, Dr. Spiegel and his colleagues found that people who are easily hypnotized tend to be more trusting of others, more intuitive, and more likely to get caught up in a good movie. The research team compared people who were highly hypnotizable with those low in hypnotizability. Both groups were given fMRI scans during several different conditions: at rest, while recalling a memory, and during two sessions of hypnotism. The researchers saw some interesting changes in the brain during hypnosis—but only in the highly hypnotizable group. Specifically, there was a drop in activity in the part of the brain which usually fires up when there is something to worry about.

This helps explain how hypnosis can have powerful effects, including reducing stress, anxiety, pain, and self-consciousness. Spiegel hopes that the practice can be used to replace painkillers. His own previous research has shown that when people in pain were taught self-hypnosis, they needed half the pain medication and suffered half the pain of those who were only given access to painkillers. However, more needs to be learned about hypnosis in order to harness its potential effects.

outline: Dr. David Spiegel 1972 年接受三小時的肩部手術後，沒有用止痛藥，(Instead) 而是自我催眠，結果奏效，除了研究催眠 45 年的他自己，大家都很驚訝。
很多人誤以為催眠像睡著一樣、別人叫你做什麼就做什麼，(But) 但 Spiegel 認為催眠是高度專注的狀態，排除周遭的刺激，可以有效控制疼痛、緩解焦慮。
每個人容易催眠的程度 (however) 並不相同：容易催眠的人比較信任別人、依賴直覺，看電影也容易入戲；研究用功能性磁振造影比較兩組人，只有容易催眠的那組在催眠時大腦出現變化。
(Specifically) 具體來說，大腦中通常在有事情要擔心時活躍的區域，活動下降了，這說明了催眠為什麼能減輕壓力、焦慮、疼痛和自我意識。
Spiegel 希望催眠能取代止痛藥：學會自我催眠的病人，止痛藥用量和疼痛程度都只有對照組的一半；(However) 不過要發揮催眠的潛力，還需要更多了解。

zh: 1972 年，David Spiegel 醫師動完三個小時的肩部手術，復原期間沒有用任何止痛藥，而是替自己催眠。結果真的有效。除了研究催眠已經 45 年的 Spiegel 本人，大家都很驚訝。
很多人誤以為催眠是一種像睡覺一樣的狀態，人在這種狀態下睡著了，別人叫他做什麼，他就做什麼。不過，根據 Spiegel 醫師的說法，催眠是一種高度專注、注意力非常集中的狀態。處在催眠狀態時，你會把周遭大部分的刺激都屏除在外，全神貫注在眼前的事情上，幾乎不去想任何別的事情。這種恍惚般的狀態，可以是控制疼痛、緩解焦慮、應付壓力的有效工具。

不過，並不是每個人都一樣容易催眠。Spiegel 醫師和同事在最近一項研究中發現，容易催眠的人往往比較信任別人，比較依賴直覺，看到一部好電影，也比較容易沉浸其中。研究團隊把很容易催眠的人和不容易催眠的人做比較，兩組人都在幾種不同的情況下接受功能性磁振造影（fMRI）掃描：休息時、回想一段記憶時，以及兩次催眠過程中。研究人員看到大腦在催眠時出現一些有趣的變化，但只出現在容易催眠的那一組。具體來說，大腦中通常在有事情要擔心時就會活躍起來的區域，活動下降了。
這有助於解釋催眠為什麼能有強大的效果，包括減輕壓力、焦慮、疼痛和自我意識。Spiegel 希望催眠可以用來取代止痛藥。他自己先前的研究顯示，身體疼痛的人學了自我催眠以後，和只用止痛藥的人相比，需要的止痛藥只有一半，感受到的疼痛也只有一半。不過，要善用催眠的潛在效果，對催眠還需要更多的了解。

title: 語言與嗅覺描述的文化差異（Cultural Differences in Language and Smell Description）
paras: In many languages, such as English, there is no straightforward way to talk about smell. For want of dedicated odor terminology, English speakers are often forced to use odor-sources such as “flowery” and “vanilla” and metaphors like “sweet” and “oriental” in their descriptions of smell.

But the difficulty with talking about smell is not universal. The Maniq, a group of hunter-gatherers in southern Thailand, can describe smells using at least fifteen different terms, which express only smells and are not applicable across other sensory domains. In addition to Maniq, researchers found that there are also a dozen words for various smells in Jahai, a language spoken by a neighboring hunter-gatherer population.

Interestingly, the difficulty for English speakers to translate smell directly into words seems to have very little to do with the nose’s actual capabilities. According to findings of a recent study, English speakers are capable of discriminating more than a trillion different odors. Then, why is there a gap between their ability to discriminate scent and their vocabulary? The researchers suggest that surroundings may play a significant role.

Maniq and Jahai speakers live in tropical rainforest regions with a hunting-gathering lifestyle, and these two ethnic groups evaluate their surroundings through their noses to survive in nature. In an environment that is still largely untouched by humans, they are surrounded by smells at all times. They need to use their sense of smell to identify animals that they can hunt, and to recognize objects or events, such as spoiled food, that can pose a danger. Unlike the Maniq and the Jahai, many English speakers inhabit the post-industrial west and do not rely on smells to survive in their environment. This difference may explain the interesting linguistic phenomenon discussed above.

outline: 英語等許多語言缺少專門的氣味詞彙，很難直接談論氣味，英語使用者常得借用 vanilla 這類氣味來源，或 sweet 這類比喻來描述。
(But) 但不是每種語言都這樣：泰國南部的狩獵採集民族 Maniq 至少有十五個專門描述氣味的詞，(In addition to) 鄰近的 Jahai 語也有十幾個。
(Interestingly) 有趣的是，英語使用者能分辨超過一兆種氣味，說不出來和鼻子的能力無關；(Then) 那麼落差從哪裡來？研究者認為環境可能扮演重要角色。
Maniq 和 Jahai 人住在熱帶雨林，隨時處在各種氣味之中，要靠嗅覺辨認可以獵捕的動物，也要察覺腐壞食物這類危險。
(Unlike) 和 Maniq、Jahai 人不同，許多英語使用者住在後工業化的西方，不必靠氣味在環境中生存，這個差異也許能解釋上面談到的語言現象。

zh: 在英語等許多語言裡，沒有直截了當談論氣味的方法。因為缺少專門的氣味詞彙，說英語的人描述氣味時，常常只好借用氣味的來源，例如「flowery」（花香的）和「vanilla」（香草的），或是用「sweet」（甜的）、「oriental」（東方的）這類比喻。
不過，談論氣味的困難並不是每種語言都有。Maniq 人是泰國南部以狩獵採集維生的一個族群，他們至少能用十五個不同的詞描述氣味，這些詞只用來表達氣味，不能用在其他的感官上。除了 Maniq 語，研究人員還發現，鄰近另一個狩獵採集族群說的 Jahai 語，也有十幾個描述各種氣味的詞。
有趣的是，說英語的人很難把氣味直接化為文字，這似乎和鼻子實際的能力沒什麼關係。根據最近一項研究的結果，說英語的人能分辨超過一兆種不同的氣味。那麼，為什麼他們分辨氣味的能力和詞彙之間，會有這樣的落差呢？研究人員認為，周遭的環境可能扮演了重要的角色。

說 Maniq 語和 Jahai 語的人住在熱帶雨林地區，過著狩獵採集的生活，這兩個族群要靠鼻子評估周遭的環境，才能在大自然中生存。在一個大部分仍未經人類開發的環境裡，他們隨時都處在各種氣味之中。他們需要用嗅覺辨認可以獵捕的動物，也要辨認會帶來危險的東西或情況，例如腐壞的食物。和 Maniq 人、Jahai 人不同，很多說英語的人住在後工業化的西方，不必靠氣味在環境中生存。這個差異或許可以解釋上面談到的有趣語言現象。

ms.t: In many languages, such as English, there is no straightforward way to talk about smell.
But the difficulty with talking about smell is not universal.
Interestingly, the difficulty for English speakers to translate smell directly into words seems to have very little to do with the nose’s actual capabilities.
This difference may explain the interesting linguistic phenomenon discussed above.

title: 霍加狓的發現、特徵與保育困境（Okapi: Discovery, Characteristics, and Conservation Challenges）
paras: The okapi is a mammal living above the equator in one of the most biodiverse areas in central Africa. The animal was unknown to the western world until the beginning of the 20th century, and is often described as half-zebra, half-giraffe, as if it were a mixed-breed creature from a Greek legend. Yet its image is prevalent in the Democratic Republic of Congo—the only country in the world where it is found living in the wild. The okapi is to Congo what the giant panda is to China or the kangaroo to Australia.

Although the okapi has striped markings resembling those of zebras’, it is most closely related to the giraffe. It has a long neck, and large, flexible ears. The face and throat are greyish white. The coat is a chocolate to reddish brown, much in contrast with the white horizontal stripes and rings on the legs and white ankles. Overall, the okapi can be easily distinguished from its nearest relative. It is much smaller (about the size of a horse), and shares more external similarities with the deer than with the giraffe. While both sexes possess horns in the giraffe, only males bear horns in the okapi.

The West got its first whiff of the okapi in 1890 when Welsh journalist Henry Morton Stanley had puzzled over a strange “African donkey” in his book. Other Europeans in Africa had also heard of an animal that they came to call the “African unicorn.” Explorers may have seen the fleeting view of the striped backside as the animal fled through the bushes, leading to speculation that the okapi was some sort of rainforest zebra. Some even believed that the okapi was a new species of zebra. It was only later, when okapi skeleton was analyzed, that naturalists realized they had a giraffe on their hands.

In 1987, the Okapi Wildlife Reserve was established in eastern Congo to protect this rare mammal. But decades of political turbulence has seen much of the Congo’s natural resources spin out of the government’s control, and okapi numbers have fallen by 50 percent since 1995. Today, only 10,000 remain.

outline: 霍加狓生活在中非，西方直到 20 世紀初才知道牠，常形容牠半斑馬半長頸鹿；(Yet) 然而在牠唯一的野生棲地剛果，牠的形象隨處可見，就像大貓熊之於中國。
(Although) 雖然霍加狓的條紋像斑馬，親緣最近的卻是長頸鹿：脖子長，耳朵大而靈活，臉和喉嚨灰白色，身體是巧克力色到紅棕色，和腿上白色的橫紋、白腳踝形成對比。
(Overall) 整體來說，霍加狓很容易和長頸鹿區分：體型小很多，大約和馬一樣大，外觀更像鹿；(While) 長頸鹿公母都有角，霍加狓只有公的有角。
西方最早在 1890 年從 Stanley 的書中聽說一種奇怪的「非洲驢」；探險家可能只瞥見牠帶條紋的臀部，有人猜是雨林斑馬，(It was only later) 直到分析骨骸，才發現是長頸鹿的親戚。
1987 年剛果東部設立霍加狓野生動物保護區，(But) 但數十年的政治動盪讓天然資源脫離政府掌控，霍加狓數量從 1995 年以來減少一半，如今只剩一萬隻。

zh: 霍加狓是一種哺乳動物，生活在赤道以北、中非生物多樣性最豐富的地區之一。一直到 20 世紀初，西方世界才知道有這種動物。人們常形容牠半斑馬、半長頸鹿，好像牠是希臘神話裡由兩種動物合成的生物。然而，在剛果民主共和國，霍加狓的形象隨處可見，剛果也是世界上唯一有野生霍加狓的國家。霍加狓對剛果的意義，就像大貓熊之於中國，袋鼠之於澳洲。
雖然霍加狓身上的條紋和斑馬很像，牠的親緣關係卻和長頸鹿最近。霍加狓的脖子很長，耳朵又大又靈活，臉和喉嚨是灰白色。身上的毛是巧克力色到紅棕色，和腿上白色的橫紋、環紋，以及白色的腳踝，形成強烈的對比。整體來說，霍加狓很容易和牠最近的親戚長頸鹿區分。霍加狓的體型小得多（大約和馬一樣大），外觀和鹿相似的地方，比和長頸鹿還多。長頸鹿公母都有角，霍加狓卻只有公的有角。

西方第一次聽到霍加狓的一點風聲，是在 1890 年。威爾斯記者 Henry Morton Stanley 在他的書裡，提到一種讓他百思不解的奇怪「非洲驢」。其他在非洲的歐洲人也聽說過一種動物，後來他們把牠稱為「非洲獨角獸」。探險家看到的，可能只是這種動物逃進樹叢時，一閃而過的條紋臀部，於是有人猜測霍加狓是某種雨林斑馬，有些人甚至相信霍加狓是一種新的斑馬。一直到後來分析了霍加狓的骨骸，博物學家才發現，他們遇到的其實是長頸鹿家族的動物。
1987 年，剛果東部設立了霍加狓野生動物保護區，保護這種稀有的哺乳動物。但是，數十年的政治動盪，讓剛果大部分的天然資源脫離了政府的掌控，霍加狓的數量從 1995 年以來減少了一半，如今只剩下一萬隻。

But decades of political turbulence has seen much of the Congo’s natural resources spin out of the government’s control, and okapi numbers have fallen by 50 percent since 1995.

title: 音樂產業的群眾募資（Crowd-funding in the Music Industry）
paras: All pop artists like to say that they owe their success to their fans. In the case of British band SVM, it’s indeed true. The band is currently recording songs because 358 fans contributed the £100,000 needed for the project. The arrangement came via MMC, an online record label that uses Web-based, social-network-style “crowd-funding” to finance its acts.

Here’s how it works: MMC posts demos and videos of 10 artists on its website, and users are invited to invest from £10 to £1,000 in the ones they most enjoy or think are most likely to become popular. Once an act reaches £100,000, the financing process is completed, and the money is used to pay for recording and possibly a concert tour. Profits from resulting music sales, concerts, and merchandise are split three ways: investors get to divide 40%; another 40% goes to MMC; the artist pockets 20%. The payoff for investors can be big. One fan in France who contributed £4,250 got his money back 22 times over.

Crowd-funding musical acts is not new. But MMC takes the concept to another level. First of all, investors can get cash rather than just goodies like free downloads or tickets. Also, MMC is a record label. It has the means to get its music distributed around the world and to market artists effectively. “Artists need professional support,” says the CEO of MMC’s international division.

While digital technology and the Net have created a do-it-yourself boom among musicians, success is still a long shot. Out of the 20,000 records released in the U.S. in 2009, only 14 DIY acts made it to the Top 200. Also, with less revenue from recorded music, music companies have become less likely to take risks, which has led to fewer artists receiving funding. The crowd-funding model, however, allows for more records to be made by spreading risk among hundreds of backers. And the social-network aspect of the site helps expand fan bases; that is, investors become a promotional army.

outline: 流行歌手常說成功要感謝歌迷，英國樂團 SVM 確實如此：358 位歌迷出資 10 萬英鎊讓他們錄音，這筆錢來自線上唱片公司 MMC 的網路「群眾募資」。
(Here’s how it works) MMC 在網站放上 10 組藝人的試聽帶，讓使用者投資 10 到 1,000 英鎊；(Once) 一旦募到 10 萬英鎊就用來錄音，收益由投資人、MMC 各分 40%，藝人拿 20%。
群眾募資並不新鮮，(But) 但 MMC 更進一步：(First of all) 第一，投資人拿到的是現金，不只是贈品；(Also) 第二，MMC 本身是唱片公司，能把音樂發行到全世界。
(While) 數位科技讓音樂人掀起自己動手做的風潮，成功仍然很難，2009 年只有 14 組 DIY 藝人進入前 200 名；(Also) 加上唱片收入減少，唱片公司更不敢冒險。
群眾募資的模式 (however) 則把風險分散給數百位投資人，讓更多唱片得以製作；網站的社群特性也幫忙擴大歌迷群，(that is) 也就是說，投資人成了宣傳大軍。

zh: 流行歌手都喜歡說，他們的成功要歸功於歌迷。以英國樂團 SVM 來說，這句話一點也不假。這個樂團正在錄製歌曲，因為有 358 位歌迷出資，籌到了這項計畫需要的 10 萬英鎊。這項安排是透過 MMC 促成的。MMC 是一家線上唱片公司，用網路上類似社群網站的「群眾募資」方式，替旗下的藝人籌措資金。

運作方式是這樣的：MMC 在網站上放 10 組藝人的試聽帶和影片，邀請使用者投資 10 到 1,000 英鎊，投給他們最喜歡、或認為最可能走紅的藝人。一組藝人募到 10 萬英鎊，籌資程序就完成了，這筆錢會用來支付錄音的費用，也可能用來辦巡迴演唱會。之後音樂銷售、演唱會和周邊商品的收益，分成三份：投資人一起分 40%，另外 40% 歸 MMC，藝人拿 20%。投資人的回報可能很高。法國有一位歌迷投資了 4,250 英鎊，拿回了 22 倍的錢。
替音樂人群眾募資並不新鮮，但 MMC 把這個概念推到了另一個層次。第一，投資人可以拿到現金，不只是免費下載或門票這類贈品。第二，MMC 本身是一家唱片公司，有能力把音樂發行到全世界，也能有效地行銷藝人。MMC 國際部門的執行長說：「藝人需要專業的支援。」
雖然數位科技和網路讓音樂人掀起了一股自己動手做（DIY）的風潮，要成功仍然很難。2009 年美國發行的兩萬張唱片中，只有 14 組自己動手做的藝人擠進前 200 名。此外，唱片的收入減少，唱片公司變得比較不敢冒險，獲得資金的藝人也就變少了。然而，群眾募資的模式把風險分散給數百位出資者，讓更多唱片能夠製作出來。網站的社群特性也有助於擴大歌迷群，也就是說，投資人成了宣傳大軍。

title: 法貝熱彩蛋的歷史與象徵意義（History and Symbolic Meaning of Fabergé Eggs）
paras: Fabergé eggs are jeweled eggs that were made by the famous Russian jeweler, the House of Fabergé, from 1885 to 1917. The eggs were made of valuable metals or stones coated with beautiful colors and decorated with precious jewels.

The first Fabergé egg was crafted for Tsar Alexander III, who gave his wife, the Empress Maria Fedorovna, an Easter egg to celebrate their 20th wedding anniversary. He placed an order with a young jeweler, Peter Carl Fabergé, whose beautiful creations had caught Maria’s eye earlier. On Easter morning of 1885, what appeared to be a simple enameled egg was delivered to the palace. But to the delight of the Empress, the egg opened to a golden yolk; within the yolk was a golden hen; and concealed within the hen was a diamond miniature of the royal crown and a tiny ruby egg. Unfortunately, the last two surprises are now lost to history.

Empress Maria was so delighted by this gift that Alexander appointed Fabergé a “goldsmith by special appointment to the Imperial Crown.” The Tsar also asked Fabergé to make an Easter egg every year. The requirements were straightforward: Each egg must be unique, and each must contain a pleasant surprise. With excellent craftsmanship and an inventive spirit, Peter Fabergé and his successors repeatedly met the challenge. The House of Fabergé made approximately 50 Imperial Easter Eggs for Tsar Alexander III and his son Nicholas II until 1917, when the Russian revolution broke out.

Today, the term “Fabergé eggs” has become a synonym of luxury and the eggs are regarded as masterpieces of the jeweler’s art. More significantly, perhaps, they serve as reminders of the last Russian imperial family.

outline: 法貝熱彩蛋是俄國著名珠寶商法貝熱公司在 1885 到 1917 年間製作的珠寶蛋，用貴重金屬或寶石做成，塗上美麗的色彩，再鑲上珍貴珠寶。
第一顆彩蛋是沙皇亞歷山大三世為了慶祝結婚 20 週年，送給皇后瑪麗亞的復活節彩蛋，他向作品曾經吸引皇后注意的年輕珠寶師 Peter Carl Fabergé 訂製。
1885 年復活節送進宮的看似普通的琺瑯蛋，(But) 打開卻讓皇后驚喜：蛋裡有金蛋黃，蛋黃裡有金母雞，母雞裡藏著鑽石小皇冠和紅寶石小蛋；(Unfortunately) 可惜最後這兩樣已經失傳。
皇后非常喜歡，沙皇於是任命法貝熱為皇室金匠，(also) 還要他每年做一顆獨一無二、藏有驚喜的復活節彩蛋；到 1917 年俄國革命為止，法貝熱和繼承人一共做了大約 50 顆。
(Today) 如今「法貝熱彩蛋」已成為奢華的代名詞，公認是珠寶藝術的傑作；(More significantly) 更重要的是，它們讓人想起俄國最後的皇室。

zh: 法貝熱彩蛋是俄國著名的珠寶商法貝熱公司（the House of Fabergé）在 1885 年到 1917 年間製作的珠寶蛋。這些彩蛋用貴重的金屬或寶石做成，塗上美麗的色彩，再鑲上珍貴的珠寶。

第一顆法貝熱彩蛋，是替沙皇亞歷山大三世製作的。沙皇為了慶祝結婚 20 週年，要送妻子瑪麗亞皇后一顆復活節彩蛋。他向年輕的珠寶師 Peter Carl Fabergé 訂製，這位珠寶師美麗的作品，先前就吸引了瑪麗亞的目光。1885 年復活節早上，一顆看起來像是普通琺瑯蛋的彩蛋送進了宮。不過，讓皇后驚喜的是，蛋打開來，裡面是一顆金蛋黃；蛋黃裡有一隻金母雞；母雞裡還藏著一頂鑽石做的小皇冠和一顆小小的紅寶石蛋。可惜的是，最後這兩樣驚喜如今已經失傳。
瑪麗亞皇后非常喜歡這份禮物，亞歷山大於是任命法貝熱為「皇室特約金匠」。沙皇也要法貝熱每年做一顆復活節彩蛋。要求很簡單：每一顆彩蛋都必須獨一無二，每一顆都要藏著令人驚喜的東西。憑著精湛的工藝和創新的精神，Peter Fabergé 和他的繼承人一次又一次達成了這項挑戰。法貝熱公司替沙皇亞歷山大三世和他的兒子尼古拉二世，做了大約 50 顆皇室復活節彩蛋，一直到 1917 年俄國革命爆發為止。
如今，「法貝熱彩蛋」已經成為奢華的代名詞，這些彩蛋公認是珠寶藝術的傑作。或許更重要的是，這些彩蛋讓人想起俄國最後的皇室。

title: 蜘蛛網的構造與絲線特性（Structure and Silk Thread Characteristics of Spider Webs）
paras: Spider webs are one of the most fascinating examples of animal architecture. The most beautiful and structurally ordered are the orb webs. The main function of the web is to intercept and hold flying prey, such as flies, bees and other insects, long enough for the spider to catch them. In order to do so, the threads of the web have to withstand the impact forces from large and heavy prey as well as environmental forces from wind and rain for at least a day in most cases.

The orb web is found to have two main characteristics. The first is its geometry, which consists of an outer frame and a central part from which threads radiate outward. Enclosed in the frame are capture spirals winding round and round from the web center out to the frame. The whole web is in tension and held in place by anchor threads, which connect the frame to the surrounding vegetation or objects. The second and perhaps most important characteristic is the material with which it is built. Spider silk is a kind of natural composite that gives this lightweight fiber a tensile strength comparable to that of steel, while at the same time making it very elastic. Two types of silk threads are used in the web. One is highly elastic and can stretch to almost twice its original length before breaking and, for most types of spiders, is covered in glue. This type is used in the capture spiral for catching and holding prey. The other is stiffer and stronger, and is used for the radius, frames and anchor threads, which allows the web to withstand prey impact and to keep its structural strength through a wide range of environmental conditions.

outline: 蜘蛛網是動物建築最迷人的例子之一，其中以圓網最美、結構最有秩序。
蜘蛛網的主要功能是攔住飛行的獵物，讓蜘蛛來得及捕捉；(In order to do so) 為了做到這一點，網絲必須承受大型獵物的撞擊和風雨，通常至少要維持一天。
圓網有兩大特點，(The first) 第一是幾何結構：外框加上從中心向外放射的絲，捕獵螺旋一圈圈從中心繞到外框，整張網再靠固定絲繫在周圍的植物或物體上。
(The second) 第二點，也可能是最重要的一點，是建材：蜘蛛絲是天然的複合材料，又輕又有和鋼相當的抗拉強度，(while) 同時又很有彈性。
網上用了兩種絲：(One) 一種彈性高，多半塗有黏液，用在捕獵螺旋；(The other) 另一種比較硬、比較強韌，用在輻射絲、外框和固定絲，讓網承受得了獵物撞擊。

zh: 蜘蛛網是動物建築中最迷人的例子之一，其中最美麗、結構最有秩序的，是圓網。蜘蛛網的主要功能，是攔住並困住蒼蠅、蜜蜂和其他昆蟲等飛行的獵物，讓蜘蛛有足夠的時間把獵物抓住。為了做到這一點，蜘蛛網的絲必須承受又大又重的獵物撞上來的衝擊力，也要承受風雨等環境的力量，大多數情況下，至少要維持一天。

研究發現，圓網有兩大特點。第一是它的幾何結構，由一個外框和一個中心組成，絲從中心向外放射。外框裡圍著捕獵螺旋，從網的中心一圈又一圈繞到外框。整張網處在繃緊的狀態，靠固定絲（anchor threads）固定在原位，固定絲把外框繫在周圍的植物或物體上。第二個特點，也可能是最重要的特點，是建造蜘蛛網的材料。蜘蛛絲是一種天然的複合材料，這種輕盈的纖維，抗拉強度和鋼差不多，同時又非常有彈性。蜘蛛網用了兩種絲。一種彈性很高，可以拉長到將近原來的兩倍才斷，大多數種類的蜘蛛，還會在這種絲上塗上黏液。這種絲用在捕獵螺旋上，用來捕捉並困住獵物。另一種絲比較硬、比較強韌，用在輻射絲、外框和固定絲上，讓蜘蛛網承受得住獵物的撞擊，在各種環境條件下都能保持結構的強度。

title: 以基因改造蚊子對抗瘧疾（Genetically Modified Mosquitoes against Malaria）
paras: Scientists are trying to genetically modify the world in which we live. They are even trying to wipe out diseases via genetic modification. For example, researchers have tried to engineer mosquitoes to kill malaria parasites. The malaria parasite is carried by the female Anopheles mosquito. When transmitted to a human, the parasite travels first to the liver and then on to the bloodstream, where it reproduces and destroys red blood cells. An estimated 250 million people suffer from malaria each year, and about one million die—many of them children. There are currently no effective or approved malaria vaccines.

To “kill” malaria, scientists are genetically modifying a bacterium in mosquitoes so that it releases toxic compounds. These compounds are not harmful to humans or the mosquito itself, but they do kill off the malaria parasite, making the mosquito incapable of infecting humans with malaria.

Despite this achievement, scientists are faced with the challenge of giving the modified mosquitoes a competitive advantage so that they can eventually replace the wild population. Complete blockage of the malaria parasite is very important. If some of the parasites slip through the mechanism, then the next generation will likely become resistant to it. And if that happens, the scientists are back where they started.

Another challenge for scientists is to gain public approval for this genetic modification regarding mosquitoes and malaria control. Environmental activists have raised concerns about the release of genetically engineered organisms without any clear knowledge of their long-term effect on ecosystems and human health. There is still a long way to go before genetic modification techniques are put to use in disease control.

outline: 科學家嘗試用基因改造改變世界，甚至消滅疾病，(For example) 例如改造蚊子來殺死瘧疾寄生蟲；寄生蟲由雌性瘧蚊攜帶，傳給人以後先到肝臟，再進入血液繁殖、破壞紅血球。
每年約有 2.5 億人感染瘧疾，約一百萬人死亡，其中很多是兒童，目前還沒有有效或核准的瘧疾疫苗。
為了「殺死」瘧疾，科學家改造蚊子體內的一種細菌，讓它釋放有毒化合物；這種化合物對人和蚊子無害，卻能殺死瘧疾寄生蟲，蚊子也就無法把瘧疾傳給人。
(Despite) 儘管有這項成果，科學家還要讓改造蚊子有競爭優勢，最終取代野生蚊子；(If) 要是有寄生蟲漏網，下一代很可能產生抗性，(And if) 一旦如此，就得從頭來過。

zh: 科學家正嘗試用基因改造來改變我們生活的世界，甚至想透過基因改造消滅疾病。例如，研究人員曾嘗試改造蚊子，讓蚊子殺死瘧疾寄生蟲。瘧疾寄生蟲由雌性瘧蚊攜帶。寄生蟲傳到人身上以後，先到肝臟，再進入血液，在血液裡繁殖，破壞紅血球。每年估計有 2.5 億人感染瘧疾，大約一百萬人死亡，其中有很多是兒童。目前還沒有有效、或經過核准的瘧疾疫苗。
為了「殺死」瘧疾，科學家正在改造蚊子體內的一種細菌，讓這種細菌釋放有毒的化合物。這些化合物對人和蚊子本身都無害，卻能殺死瘧疾寄生蟲，讓蚊子無法把瘧疾傳給人。
儘管有這項成果，科學家還要面對一個挑戰：讓改造過的蚊子具有競爭優勢，最後能取代野生的蚊子。完全阻斷瘧疾寄生蟲非常重要。要是有一些寄生蟲從這個機制中漏網，下一代很可能就會產生抗性。一旦發生這種情況，科學家就得從頭來過。
科學家的另一個挑戰，是讓大眾認同這項針對蚊子和瘧疾防治的基因改造。環保人士提出疑慮，擔心在還不清楚基因改造生物對生態系和人體健康有什麼長期影響的情況下，就把它們野放出去。基因改造技術要用在疾病防治上，還有很長的路要走。

title: 德萊斯的滑行車與自行車的起源（Karl Drais’s Running Machine and the Origin of the Bicycle）
paras: Born in 1785 in southwestern Germany, Baron Karl Drais was one of the most creative German inventors of the 19th century. The baron’s numerous inventions include, among others, the earliest typewriter, the meat grinder, a device to record piano music on paper, and two four-wheeled human-powered vehicles. But it was the running machine, the modern ancestor of the bicycle, that made him famous.

The running machine, also called Draisine or hobby horse, was in effect a very primitive bicycle: it had no chains and was propelled by riders pushing off the ground with their feet. Though not a bike in the modern sense of the word, Drais’ invention marked the big bang for the bicycle’s development. It was the first vehicle with two wheels placed in line. The frame and wheels were made of wood; the steering already resembled a modern handlebar. Drais’ big democratic idea behind his invention was to find a muscle-powered replacement for the horses, which were expensive and consumed lots of food even when not in use. The machine, he believed, would allow large numbers of people faster movement than walking or riding in a coach.

Drais undertook his first documented ride on June 12, 1817, covering a distance of 13 kilometers in one hour. A few months later, Drais created a huge sensation when he rode 60 kilometers in four hours. These were later followed by a marketing trip to Paris, where the hobby horse quickly caught on. The fad also quickly spread to Britain.

The success of the hobby horse was short-lived, though. They were heavy and difficult to ride. Safety was an issue, too: They lacked a brake, as well as cranks and pedals. There were frequent collisions with unsuspecting pedestrians, and after a few years Drais’ invention was banned in many European and American cities. Drais’ ideas, however, did not disappear entirely. Decades later, the machine was equipped by Frenchmen Pierre Lallement and Pierre Michaux with pedals to become the modern bicycle.

outline: 1785 年生於德國的德萊斯男爵是 19 世紀德國最有創意的發明家之一，發明過最早的打字機、絞肉機等，(But) 但讓他成名的是自行車的始祖「滑行車」。
滑行車沒有鏈條，靠騎士用腳蹬地前進，(Though) 雖然不算現代意義的自行車，卻是自行車發展的起點：它是第一輛兩輪前後排列的車，轉向裝置已經很像現代的把手。
德萊斯的構想是用人力取代昂貴、不用時也要吃很多飼料的馬，讓一般大眾移動得比走路或坐馬車快。
1817 年 6 月 12 日他首次有紀錄的試騎，一小時騎了 13 公里，(A few months later) 幾個月後四小時騎了 60 公里，轟動一時；之後到巴黎推銷，滑行車很快流行起來，也傳到英國。
滑行車的成功 (though) 卻很短暫：車子笨重，沒有煞車和踏板，常撞上路人，幾年後許多城市禁止使用；德萊斯的構想 (however) 並沒有消失，(Decades later) 數十年後法國人加上踏板，成了現代自行車。

zh: 德萊斯男爵（Baron Karl Drais）1785 年生於德國西南部，是 19 世紀德國最有創意的發明家之一。他的發明很多，包括最早的打字機、絞肉機、一種把鋼琴音樂記錄在紙上的裝置，還有兩種用人力推動的四輪車。不過，讓他成名的，是現代自行車的始祖：滑行車（running machine）。

滑行車又叫 Draisine 或 hobby horse，其實就是一種非常原始的自行車：沒有鏈條，靠騎的人用腳蹬地前進。雖然不是現代意義上的自行車，德萊斯的發明卻是自行車發展的重大起點。滑行車是第一輛兩個輪子前後排成一直線的車。車架和輪子都是木頭做的，轉向裝置已經很像現代的把手。德萊斯發明滑行車，背後有一個讓一般大眾都能受益的遠大構想：找一種靠人力的交通工具來取代馬，因為馬很貴，不用的時候也要吃很多飼料。他認為，這種車能讓許多人移動得比走路或坐馬車更快。
1817 年 6 月 12 日，德萊斯第一次有紀錄的試騎，一個小時騎了 13 公里。幾個月後，他四個小時騎了 60 公里，轟動一時。之後他到巴黎推銷，滑行車很快就在巴黎流行起來，這股熱潮也很快傳到英國。
不過，滑行車的成功很短暫。這種車很重，也很難騎。安全也是問題：沒有煞車，也沒有曲柄和踏板。滑行車常常撞上沒有防備的行人，幾年以後，歐洲和美國的許多城市都禁止使用德萊斯的發明。然而，德萊斯的構想並沒有完全消失。數十年後，法國人 Pierre Lallement 和 Pierre Michaux 替滑行車裝上踏板，成了現代的自行車。

title: Li-Fi技術的優勢與應用（Advantages and Applications of Li-Fi Technology）
paras: Flickering lamps can induce headaches. But if the flickering happens millions of times a second—far faster than the eye can see or the brain process—then it might be harnessed to do something useful, like transmitting data. This is the idea behind Li-Fi, or Light Fidelity. The term Li-Fi was coined by University of Edinburgh Professor Harald Haas in a 2011 TED Talk, where he introduced the idea of “wireless data from every light.” Today, Li-Fi has developed into a wireless technology that allows data to be sent at high speeds, working with light-emitting diodes (LEDs), an increasingly popular way to illuminate public areas and homes.

Using LED lights as networking devices for data transmission, Li-Fi has several advantages over Wi-Fi (Wireless Fidelity). First, Li-Fi allows for greater security on local networks, as light cannot penetrate walls or doors, unlike radio waves used in Wi-Fi. As long as transparent materials like glass windows are covered, access to a Li-Fi channel is limited to devices inside the room, ensuring that signals cannot be hacked from remote locations. Also, Li-Fi can operate in electromagnetic sensitive areas such as aircraft cabins, hospitals, and nuclear power plants, for light does not interfere with radio signals. The most significant advantage of Li-Fi is speed. Researchers have achieved speeds of 224 gigabits per second in lab conditions, much faster than Wi-Fi broadband.

How could Li-Fi enrich daily life? Anywhere there is LED lighting, there is an opportunity for Li-Fi enabled applications. Li-Fi-enabled street lights could provide internet access to mobile phones, making walking at night safer. The LED bulbs in traffic lights could provide drivers with weather conditions and traffic updates. Li-Fi could help with tourism by providing an easier access to local information. At home, smart light could also provide parents with solutions to their children’s Internet addiction: Just turn off the lights and you’ve turned off their access.
When 14 billion light bulbs mean 14 billion potential transmitters of wireless data, a cleaner, a greener, and even a brighter future is on the way.

outline: 閃爍的燈會讓人頭痛，(But) 但如果每秒閃爍數百萬次，快到察覺不到，就能用來傳輸資料，這就是 Li-Fi（光照上網），由 Harald Haas 教授在 2011 年的 TED 演講中提出。
(Today) 如今 Li-Fi 已經發展成一種無線技術，搭配越來越常用來照明公共場所和住家的 LED 燈，高速傳送資料。
Li-Fi 比 Wi-Fi 有幾項優勢：(First) 第一，光線穿不透牆壁，(unlike) 不像 Wi-Fi 的無線電波，所以不怕遠端駭客入侵；(Also) 第二，光線不會干擾無線電訊號，可以用在機艙、醫院等對電磁敏感的地方。
(The most significant advantage) 最大的優勢是速度，實驗室裡已經達到每秒 224 gigabits，比 Wi-Fi 寬頻快得多。
有 LED 照明的地方就能應用 Li-Fi：路燈讓手機上網，紅綠燈提供駕駛路況，家長關燈就能切斷孩子的網路；140 億顆燈泡就是 140 億個潛在的資料發射器。

zh: 閃爍的燈會讓人頭痛。不過，如果燈一秒鐘閃爍幾百萬次，遠遠快過眼睛看得到、大腦處理得了的速度，也許就能用來做有用的事，例如傳輸資料。這就是 Li-Fi（Light Fidelity，光照上網）背後的構想。Li-Fi 這個名詞，是愛丁堡大學的 Harald Haas 教授在 2011 年的一場 TED 演講中創造的，他在演講中提出「每一盞燈都能傳送無線資料」的構想。今天，Li-Fi 已經發展成一種能高速傳送資料的無線技術，搭配的是發光二極體（LED），LED 也越來越常用來照明公共場所和住家。

Li-Fi 用 LED 燈當作傳輸資料的網路裝置，比起 Wi-Fi（Wireless Fidelity，無線上網）有幾項優勢。第一，Li-Fi 讓區域網路更安全，因為光線穿不透牆壁或門，不像 Wi-Fi 用的無線電波。只要把玻璃窗等透明的材料遮住，能連上 Li-Fi 頻道的，就只有房間裡的裝置，可以確保駭客無法從遠端入侵。第二，Li-Fi 可以在對電磁敏感的地方運作，例如機艙、醫院和核電廠，因為光線不會干擾無線電訊號。Li-Fi 最大的優勢是速度。研究人員在實驗室的條件下，已經達到每秒 224 gigabits 的速度，比 Wi-Fi 寬頻快得多。
Li-Fi 能怎樣豐富日常生活呢？只要有 LED 照明的地方，就有機會應用 Li-Fi。能使用 Li-Fi 的路燈，可以讓手機上網，夜間走路也就更安全。紅綠燈裡的 LED 燈泡，可以提供駕駛天氣狀況和最新路況。Li-Fi 能讓人更容易取得當地的資訊，對觀光也有幫助。在家裡，智慧燈光還能幫家長解決孩子網路成癮的問題：只要把燈關掉，孩子就上不了網。
當 140 億顆燈泡代表 140 億個可能的無線資料發射器，一個更乾淨、更環保，甚至更光明的未來，就快到來了。

Using LED lights as networking devices for data transmission, Li-Fi has several advantages over Wi-Fi (Wireless Fidelity).
Anywhere there is LED lighting, there is an opportunity for Li-Fi enabled applications.

title: 氣候變暖讓大型甲蟲變小（Large Beetles Shrinking with Climate Warming）
paras: Some of the world’s largest beetles are getting smaller because their habitats are warming up, according to new research from the University of British Columbia, Canada. The study, published in the Journal of Animal Ecology in January 2018, shows that climate change is having an impact on these “teeny tiny” organisms.

The study began with a deep dive into the scientific literature. Evolutionary ecologist Michelle Tseng and her students combed through all the articles they could find, looking for laboratory studies of temperature effects on insects. They found 19 that indicated at least 22 beetle species shrank when raised in warmer than normal temperatures.

To see whether this pattern held true in the wild, the team made use of the university’s 600,000-specimen insect collection, which included thousands of bugs collected locally since the late 1800s. The researchers took photographs of more than 6,500 beetles from the eight species with the most extensive records. They also looked at climate records to determine trends in rainfall and other factors besides temperature. Sorting the beetles into size categories, they found that five of the eight species have shrunk over the past century. The four largest species of beetles, including the snail-killer ground beetles, shrank 20% in the past 45 years. In contrast, smaller beetles were unaffected or even slightly increased in size.

Some ecologists are cautious about Tseng’s findings, saying that it hasn’t yet been proved whether the warming temperatures are the actual cause for the beetle shrinkage. UK biologist Alan Ronan Baudron, however, is convinced. Baudron’s studies have documented shrinkage of certain fish species due to climate warming. His account is that warmer temperatures lower the concentration of oxygen in the water, causing fish to burn energy faster and mature at a smaller size. But neither he nor Tseng is convinced that decreased oxygen can explain the shrinkage in the beetles.

outline: 根據英屬哥倫比亞大學的新研究，世界上一些最大型的甲蟲因為棲地變暖而變小，研究 2018 年 1 月發表於《動物生態學期刊》，顯示氣候變遷正在影響這些小生物。
研究先查閱科學文獻，演化生態學家 Michelle Tseng 和學生找出探討溫度影響昆蟲的實驗室研究，發現至少 22 種甲蟲在比正常溫暖的環境中長大時體型縮小。
為了確認野外是否也是這樣，團隊利用學校的昆蟲標本，拍攝 8 個物種、超過 6,500 隻甲蟲，發現 8 種中有 5 種在過去一百年縮小，最大的 4 種在過去 45 年縮小了 20%。
(In contrast) 相反地，較小的甲蟲沒有縮小，甚至稍微變大。
有些生態學家認為還無法證明暖化就是原因；英國生物學家 Alan Ronan Baudron (however) 則深信如此，他記錄過某些魚類因暖化縮小，(But) 不過他和 Tseng 都不認為氧氣減少能解釋甲蟲縮小。

zh: 根據加拿大英屬哥倫比亞大學的新研究，世界上一些最大型的甲蟲正在變小，因為牠們的棲地正在變暖。這項研究 2018 年 1 月發表在《動物生態學期刊》（Journal of Animal Ecology），顯示氣候變遷正在影響這些「小不點」生物。
這項研究從深入查閱科學文獻開始。演化生態學家 Michelle Tseng 和她的學生，把找得到的論文全部仔細看過一遍，尋找探討溫度對昆蟲影響的實驗室研究。他們找到 19 篇，顯示至少有 22 種甲蟲在比正常溫暖的環境中飼養時，體型會縮小。

為了確認野外是不是也有這種現象，研究團隊利用學校收藏的 60 萬件昆蟲標本，其中包括 1800 年代末以來在當地採集的數千隻蟲子。研究人員從紀錄最完整的 8 個物種中，拍攝了超過 6,500 隻甲蟲的照片。他們也查看氣候紀錄，找出降雨量等溫度以外其他因素的變化趨勢。研究人員把甲蟲依體型分類，發現 8 種甲蟲中有 5 種在過去一百年縮小了。最大的 4 種甲蟲，包括捕食蝸牛的步行蟲，在過去 45 年縮小了 20%。相反地，比較小的甲蟲體型沒有縮小，甚至還稍微變大。
有些生態學家對 Tseng 的發現持保留態度，他們說，還沒有證明暖化就是甲蟲縮小的真正原因。不過，英國生物學家 Alan Ronan Baudron 對此深信不疑。Baudron 的研究記錄過某些魚類因為氣候暖化而縮小。他的解釋是，溫度升高讓水中的氧氣濃度降低，魚燃燒能量的速度變快，體型還比較小就成熟了。不過，他和 Tseng 都不認為氧氣減少能解釋甲蟲縮小的現象。

The study began with a deep dive into the scientific literature.
To see whether this pattern held true in the wild, the team made use of the university’s 600,000-specimen insect collection, which included thousands of bugs collected locally since the late 1800s.

title: 斯瓦巴全球種子庫的爭議（The Debate over the Svalbard Global Seed Vault）
paras: In order to protect the diversity of crops from catastrophe, the Svalbard Global Seed Vault, a seed bank, was built beneath a mountain on an Arctic island halfway between Norway and the North Pole. The Vault is meant to help farmers and scientists find the genes they need to improve today’s crops. It also aims to breed varieties that might better respond to emerging challenges, such as climate change and population growth. Currently, the Vault holds more than 860,000 samples, originating from almost every country in the world.

There is now, however, a growing body of opinion that the world’s faith in Svalbard is misplaced. Those who have worked with farmers in the field say that diversity cannot be boxed up and saved in a single container—no matter how secure it may be. Crops are always changing, pests and diseases are always adapting, and global warming will bring additional challenges that remain unforeseen. In a perfect world, the solution would be as diverse and dynamic as plant life itself.

The dispute about how best to save crop diversity centers on whether we should work with communities in the fields or with institutions, since it will be extremely difficult to find enough funding to do both. Now the isolated Svalbard seed vault is sucking up available funding. Yet, the highly centralized approach may not be able to help farmers cope with climate change, fifty or a hundred years from now. According to new research findings, as much as 75 percent of global crop diversity exists outside the big institutional seed banks. Such diversity is held instead by some of the world’s most marginal farmers. Moreover, it is argued with increasing force that seed banks can neither make up for the practical knowledge of farmers on the ground, nor compete with their ingenuity.

outline: 為了保護作物多樣性免於浩劫，斯瓦巴全球種子庫建在北極一座島嶼的山裡，幫助農民和科學家找到改良作物的基因，(also) 也希望培育出更能因應氣候變遷的品種。
(however) 然而越來越多人認為，世界對斯瓦巴的信心放錯了地方：多樣性沒辦法裝箱存在單一容器裡，因為作物不斷改變，病蟲害不斷適應，暖化還會帶來無法預見的挑戰。
爭議的焦點是保存作物多樣性應該和田間社群合作，還是和機構合作，(since) 因為經費很難兩邊都顧到；現在偏遠的斯瓦巴種子庫正吸走可用的經費。
(Yet) 然而這種高度集中的做法，五十年或一百年後可能幫不了農民因應氣候變遷；新研究發現，全球多達 75% 的作物多樣性不在大型機構種子庫，而在世界上最邊緣的一些農民手中。
(Moreover) 此外，越來越多人主張，種子庫 (neither … nor) 既無法取代第一線農民的實務知識，也比不上他們的巧思。

zh: 為了保護作物的多樣性，不受浩劫毀滅，斯瓦巴全球種子庫這座種子銀行，建在北極一座島嶼的山底下，這座島嶼位在挪威和北極點的中間。種子庫的用意，是幫助農民和科學家找到改良現有作物所需要的基因。種子庫也希望培育出更能因應新挑戰的品種，例如氣候變遷和人口成長。目前，種子庫保存了超過 86 萬份樣本，來自世界上幾乎每一個國家。
然而，現在有越來越多人認為，世界對斯瓦巴種子庫的信心放錯了地方。曾經在田間和農民一起工作的人說，多樣性沒辦法裝箱，存放在單一的容器裡，不管這個容器有多安全都一樣。作物不斷在改變，病蟲害不斷在適應，全球暖化還會帶來更多目前無法預見的挑戰。在理想的世界裡，解決的方法應該像植物本身一樣多樣、一樣不斷變化。

怎麼保存作物多樣性最好，爭議的焦點在於：我們應該和田間的社群合作，還是和機構合作，因為經費非常難找，很難兩邊都做。現在，偏遠的斯瓦巴種子庫正吸走可用的經費。然而，這種高度集中的做法，五十年或一百年後，可能沒辦法幫助農民因應氣候變遷。根據新的研究結果，全球多達 75% 的作物多樣性，存在於大型機構的種子庫之外，掌握在世界上一些最邊緣的農民手中。此外，越來越多人強力主張，種子庫既無法取代第一線農民的實務知識，也比不上他們的巧思。

The dispute about how best to save crop diversity centers on whether we should work with communities in the fields or with institutions, since it will be extremely difficult to find enough funding to do both.

title: 札哈·哈蒂的藝術生涯與建築理念（Zaha Hadid's Artistic Career and Architectural Philosophy）
paras: Often named as the most prominent contemporary female architect, Zaha Hadid, an Iraqi-born British woman, is significant for her intellectual toughness and her refusal to compromise on her artistic ideas. For many years, her designs filled the pages of architecture journals but were dismissed as impractical or too radical. Also, being female in a male-dominated field didn’t help her succeed.

Despite these setbacks, her star began to rise when her design for Cincinnati’s new Center for Contemporary Art was selected and built, earning her worldwide acclaim. The New York Times described the building as “the most important new building in America since the Cold War.” Once her talent was recognized, commissions started coming in to design a variety of projects, including public transportation, libraries, and opera houses. In 2004, Hadid became the first woman to win the prestigious Pritzker Prize. She also won the Stirling Prize in 2010 and 2011.

Hadid’s interest in architecture had roots in a trip her family took to the ancient Sumer region in southern Iraq, the site of one of the world’s oldest civilizations, when she was a teenager. She recalled: “The beauty of the landscape—where sand, water, reeds, birds, buildings, and people all somehow flowed together—has never left me. I’m trying to discover—invent, I suppose—an architecture, and forms of urban planning, that do something of the same thing in a contemporary way.”

Nature’s forms appear as a recurrent source of inspiration for Hadid’s architecture. Her designs are daring and visionary experiments with space and with the relationships of buildings to their urban surroundings. She consistently pushes the boundaries of architecture and urban design in the pursuit of a visionary aesthetic that expresses her ideals.

outline: 札哈·哈蒂是伊拉克出生的英國建築師，常有人稱她是當代最傑出的女性建築師；多年來她的設計常登上建築期刊，(but) 卻常讓人覺得不切實際、太過激進，(Also) 身為男性主導領域裡的女性，也不利於她成功。
(Despite) 儘管有這些挫折，她設計的辛辛那提當代藝術中心獲選並落成，讓她聲名大噪，《紐約時報》稱這棟建築是冷戰以來美國最重要的新建築。
(Once) 才華獲得肯定以後，大眾運輸、圖書館、歌劇院等各類設計委託接踵而來；2004 年她成為第一位獲得普立茲克獎的女性，(also) 也在 2010 和 2011 年獲得斯特林獎。
她對建築的興趣源自青少年時期到伊拉克南部古蘇美地區旅行，那裡沙、水、蘆葦、建築和人融為一體，她希望用當代的方式創造出同樣效果的建築。
自然的形態一再成為她的靈感來源，她的設計大膽而有遠見，探索空間以及建築和城市環境的關係，不斷突破建築與都市設計的界限，追求表達自身理想的美學。

zh: 札哈·哈蒂是在伊拉克出生的英國女性，常有人稱她是當代最傑出的女性建築師。她之所以重要，是因為她思想強韌，又絕不在藝術理念上妥協。多年來，她的設計常常登上建築期刊，卻也常常讓人覺得不切實際、太過激進而不予理會。此外，在男性主導的領域裡身為女性，對她的成功也沒有幫助。
儘管遇到這些挫折，她設計的辛辛那提新當代藝術中心獲選並且落成，讓她贏得全世界的讚譽，她從此開始走紅。《紐約時報》說這棟建築是「冷戰以來美國最重要的新建築」。她的才華一旦獲得肯定，各式各樣的設計委託就接踵而來，包括大眾運輸、圖書館和歌劇院。2004 年，哈蒂成為第一位獲得聲望崇高的普立茲克獎的女性。她也在 2010 年和 2011 年獲得斯特林獎。
哈蒂對建築的興趣，源自她青少年時期全家到伊拉克南部古蘇美地區的一趟旅行，那裡是世界上最古老的文明之一的所在地。她回憶說：「那裡的風景很美，沙、水、蘆葉、鳥、建築和人，都以某種方式融為一體，這片風景一直留在我心裡。我想找出──或者說創造出──一種建築和都市規劃的形式，用當代的方式做到同樣的事。」
大自然的形態一再成為哈蒂建築的靈感來源。她的設計是大膽而有遠見的實驗，探索空間，也探索建築和周圍城市環境的關係。她不斷突破建築和都市設計的界限，追求一種有遠見、能表達她理想的美學。

Despite these setbacks, her star began to rise when her design for Cincinnati’s new Center for Contemporary Art was selected and built, earning her worldwide acclaim.
Hadid’s interest in architecture had roots in a trip her family took to the ancient Sumer region in southern Iraq, the site of one of the world’s oldest civilizations, when she was a teenager.
